LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Here's how to watch, what to know, and an expert prediction before the Pats and Bears face off in Chicago Getty Images In the Week 7 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Chicago Bears play host to the New England Patriots . Chicago is coming off a win in Caleb Williams ' return to the lineup, having held on for a 31-23 victory in a game that moved the Bears to 4-2 on the season. The Bears bounced back from their dispiriting loss to the division rival Green Bay Packers the week before, when the offense looked like a disaster with backup Tyson Bagent under center. Chicago will look to keep the good times rolling here. New England also won what -- on the surface -- looked like a close game against the New York Jets , but finished with a seven-point margin of victory thanks only to a late field goal. The Patriots have won three consecutive games after starting the season 1-2, and their quarterback has found a groove after looking nearly broken to start the year. The Pats, too, are looking to keep the train on the tracks on Thursday night. Will the Bears capture another win, or will the Patriots continue their hot streak? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Bears vs. Patriots live Date: Thursday, Oct. 22 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: Soldier Field (Chicago) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bears -3, O/U 50.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Patriots have the ball Drake Maye has found himself over the last three weeks, completing 66 of 103 passes for 878 yards, 10 touchdowns, and one interception after going just 51-of-80 for 585 yards, one touchdown, and six picks through the first three games of the season. Maye has rediscovered the deep ball, in particular, going 12 of 20 for 350 yards and four scores on throws beyond 15 yards in the last three games, per Tru Media. Before that, he was just 9 of 20 for 281 yards and four interceptions on those throws. Maye finished with a strong game against the Jets despite A.J. Brown looking horrifyingly bad in his return from an ankle injury. Brown dropped (at least) three passes and turned his 10 targets into only 27 yards. Maye also lost Romeo Doubs to a shoulder injury on an early-game touchdown pass, so he was working with a limited receiving corps behind Brown. Still, he threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns without turning the ball over. Brown will presumably be better here, and Chicago hasn't been great against outside receivers, but last week's return of Kyler Gordon could lead to slot man Demario Douglas having a tougher go of things than he has over the last few weeks. Kyle Williams could get in on the action with Doubs sidelined, though Efton Chism has been getting more snaps because the Patriots trust him as a blocker. Chicago checks in a surprising eighth in opponents' EPA per dropback so far this season, per Tru Media, thanks to a high sack rate and a few timely interceptions. Opponents have averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the Bears, though, indicating that you can indeed move the ball through the air if you can get a pass off and avoid a turnover. Defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has generated pressure at an above-average rate (39.7% of dropbacks) despite working with a somewhat limited group up front, and the Patriots will be without two starting guards here. So, the running backs (particularly Rhamondre Stevenson ) will have to be on their game in pass protection on Thursday night. The Patriots have struggled to run the ball thus far this season, with Stevenson, TreVeyon Henderson and Corey Kiner combining for an average of just 3.9 yards per carry on 151 rushing attempts. Stevenson leads the way in the backfield largely because the Patriots trust him the most in short yardage and pass protection, but he hasn't been efficient or explosive. Henderson had an explosive rushing touchdown on his first run of the season but has failed to record one since. Kiner was a little-used third-stringer until he salted away the game against the Jets last Sunday. He could perhaps work his way into more touches after a nice showing in that game, given the rushing struggles of the two leads and the fact that Henderson also fumbled against New York. The Bears have allowed opponents 4.4 yards per carry on running-back rushes so far this season, with much of the success coming by way of yards before contact. It may be difficult for the Patriots to generate those types of yards with their injury issues along the offensive line, and their backs haven't exactly done the best job of breaking tackles this year, so the challenge of moving the offense down the field will likely fall squarely on Maye's right shoulder. When the Bears have the ball Caleb Williams returned last week from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury and looked no worse for wear. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown. The Bears kept things simple for him with a 3.9-yard average depth of throw (eighth-lowest for any quarterback in a single game this season), per Tru Media, and he was extremely efficient as a result. Williams has only played in three games so far this year, but he's leading the league with a 72.5% completion rate and is up to a career-best 7.8 yards per attempt. And that's despite a truly awful game against the Vikings in Week 2, where he went 15-of-26 for just 138 yards and an interception. In his first couple of appearances, it seemed like journeyman wideout Kalif Raymond (14 targets in Weeks 1 and 2) was his primary option, but on Sunday, it was Luther Burden III and Colston Loveland -- the most expected options -- leading the way with eight and seven targets, respectively. Rome Odunze saw five looks. Given the way they're each deployed, it seems likely that Odunze will see a bunch of Christian Gonzalez 's coverage on Thursday night -- especially with Carlton Davis III ruled out. Odunze is the biggest of the trio and plays most often on the perimeter, and he also tends to run the most routes. If that's the way things go, we should expect the passing game to flow through Burden and Loveland yet again. The Patriots have allowed opponents to complete 31 of 46 passes for 301 yards on throws to the slot this season, per Tru Media. Burden could have a nice night working inside if he's on the field more often than he was last week (eight targets on only 18 routes), though Marcus Jones does have an interception this season and is allowing only 1.46 yards per coverage snap in the slot, per Pro Football Focus. By contrast, New England has allowed only 29 catches for 279 yards to tight ends to date, so Loveland may not find the coverage as friendly. The Bears would do well to line him up all over the formation rather than solely in line, and perhaps use multi-tight end sets where he plays more of a receiver role, and Cole Kmet or Sam Roush handles the blocking aspects of the position. The Bears also tried against Atlanta to do what they do best: run the ball with volume. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson (the latter filling in for the injured Kyle Monangai ) combined for 29 carries. They ran for only 96 yards on those totes, but they did find the end zone three times. Chicago's offensive line actually created some nice push, generating 1.45 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media, but the backs slumped to only 1.83 yards after contact, as they combined for only four broken tackles. (For context, consider that the Seahawks ' running backs combined for 10 in their awful game against the Broncos on Thursday night.) The Pats have allowed only 3.9 yards per rush this season, thanks in part to yielding an average of only 0.75 yards before contact. Swift and Johnson (Monangai is out again) will have to do a better job of breaking tackles this time around if they want to generate yardage and create favorable down-and-distance scenarios for Williams and the passing game. I see this being a high-scoring game, what with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images What did we learn in Week 6? The Houston Texans are officially back, as is Caleb Williams with the Chicago Bears , and we have some serious questions about the Los Angeles Rams , who were upset by the Arizona Cardinals at home last Sunday. The Cardinals now have more wins at SoFi Stadium this year than the Rams and Los Angeles Chargers combined. This week, the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints will play the first-ever NFL game in Paris, the San Francisco 49ers look to remain perfect against the Atlanta Falcons , and Kenneth Walker III aims to lead the Kansas City Chiefs to victory over his former team, the Seattle Seahawks . This could be a revenge game for the ages. Which teams should you pick in Week 7, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Oct. 21 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. New England Patriots at Chicago Bears (-3) (TNF) Dajani (Bears -3): I can't remember the last time I've been this excited for a Thursday night game. Caleb Williams will suit up for the first time at home since his hamstring injury, and this is the first Bears home game since the passing of Mike Ditka. I have concerns about this Bears pass defense and how it will fare against a red-hot Drake Maye , but the fact is that Chicago has allowed 9.3 points per game at home this season. The Bears' offense has also averaged 35 points per game in their four wins, and I think Williams is out to make a statement. This will be a high-flying affair that comes down to the very end, and a push is very much in play. But give me Chicago at home, with the backing of an emotionally charged atmosphere. Remember, the Bears' lone Super Bowl win came against the New England Patriots under Ditka. … Prediction: Bears 28, Patriots 24 Dubin (Bears -3): I also see this being a high-scoring game, with two offenses that can pile up points quickly. Chicago's offense in two non-rain/non-Brian Flores games with Caleb Williams under center has been electric, particularly on the ground, and Caleb Williams opens things up for the passing game. New England is struggling to run the ball, but Drake Maye has been on fire as of late. I'll lean toward the Bears here because of the Patriots' injury issues along the offensive line, which could hold the run game back further and put even more on Maye's shoulders. … Prediction: Bears 31, Patriots 27 Pittsburgh Steelers (-3.5) vs. New Orleans Saints (Paris) Dajani (Saints +3.5): The Steelers are impossible to figure out. From week-to-week — or even half-to-half, as evidenced by last week's overtime victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . If you're going to give me the hook at +3.5 in an international game, I'm probably going to take it. The Saints are a perfect 8-0 ATS in their last eight games away from home, and are 3-0 ATS all-time in international games. I think Gayle Benson's recent comments stirred up the locker room, and the Saints responded with a win in which they dropped 34 points — even if it came against the New York Giants . … Prediction: Steelers 23, Saints 20 Dubin (Steelers -3.5): The Saints finally played a game from ahead last week against the Giants, and they didn't necessarily look comfortable doing it. They have mostly been a second-half offensive team throughout this season, struggling early on before piling up yards and points in comeback mode. I don't trust this offense enough to build a lead against Pittsburgh's defense (ninth in yards, 12th in points, fifth in EPA per play) right now, so I'll lean toward this game playing out in a similar fashion to New Orleans' early-season contests, with the Steelers taking a lead and the Saints trying to stage a comeback, only to fail this time around. … Prediction: Steelers 21, Saints 17 San Francisco 49ers (-3) at Atlanta Falcons Dajani (Falcons +3): I'm thinking about backing the Falcons in this spot. The 49ers had an emotional victory over the Seahawks in Week 5 and are now on a short week after Monday night's win against the Washington Commanders . It looked like we were in for a blowout after the 49ers went up 23-3, but Washington then outscored San Francisco, 14-0, while outgaining the 49ers 201 yards to 7 yards. The New England Patriots and Drake Maye are riding a three-game winning streak into their primetime matchup with the Chicago Bears and former No. 1 overall pick Caleb Williams on Thursday Night Football. Williams is making his second straight start after he missed three games earlier this season with a hamstring injury. The star quarterback showed no signs of rust in Week 6, completing 30 of his 36 pass attempts in a win over the Atlanta Falcons, improving the Bears to 4-2 this season. Chicago is favored in this matchup, and it needs every win it can get with the NFC North sporting four teams over .500 through the first six weeks. The Bears may be getting a little extra love in this matchup because of all the injuries for the Patriots, who have been decimated at receiver (Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs on IR) and on their offensive line. Still, New England has won three games in a row, and Maye is back in the MVP conversation with 10 touchdown passes during that streak. He has a tough matchup ahead against a Chicago team that is in the top 10 in the league in EPA/Play and success rate on defense this season. So, how should bettors attack Thursday’s showdown? In the leadup to this marquee matchup, the SI Betting team has made a bunch of game picks, prop bet selections and more. I’ve decided to share some of our favorites all in one place to help bettors get the most of this primetime matchup between two playoff contenders in Week 7. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Patriots vs. Bears Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook New England Patriots vs. Chicago Bears UNDER 50.5 (-105) – Iain MacMillan Drake Maye OVER 1.5 Passing Touchdowns (-116) – Peter Dewey Colston Loveland Anytime TD (+170) – Peter Dewey D’Andre Swift UNDER 61.5 Rushing Yards (-115) – Peter Dewey This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shared his favorite bet for this matchup in his Road to 272 column , where he picks every game of the NFL season. He’s taking the UNDER even with two star quarterbacks facing off: Unless I'm missing something, I'm not quite sure why the total for this game is in the 50s. Sure, the Bears' offense is much more explosive with Caleb Williams at quarterback, but even with that being the case, these two offenses rank 12th and 14th in EPA per play this season and seventh and 12th in success rate. A high total would make sense if the two defenses in this game were bad, but they rank in the top half of the league in most metrics. In fact, the Bears' defense comes into this game ranking fourth in opponent success rate. The Patriots' offense is also dealing with some injuries. A.J. Brown is questionable, and Romeo Doubs is on IR. Their run game can't be relied on to help out the injuries at wide receiver, as it's been largely ineffective all season. I'll bet the UNDER on Thursday Night Football for the second straight week. Maye started the season in an awful slump, throwing just one score and six picks in his first three games. Since then, he’s flipped the script, tossing 10 scores (at least three in each game) over the last three weeks, leading New England to wins over Buffalo, Las Vegas and the New York Jets. Maye is right back in the mix to win the MVP, and I like this matchup against a Chicago defense that has allowed nine passing scores in 2026 and was torched by Bryce Young and Jordan Love already this season. The Bears have benefitted from some soft scheduling in terms of the quarterbacks they’ve faced, but Love threw for 367 yards against them in Week 5, and Chicago has allowed the 15th-most passing yards in the league. New England loves to throw the ball, and I think the odds for this prop are pretty favorable considering the fact that Maye threw 31 touchdown passes in 2025. Bears tight end Colston Loveland had a breakout showing in Week 6, catching six of his seven targets for 65 yards and a score. Williams only threw one touchdown in Week 6, but Loveland was targeted multiple times in the end zone – Caleb just missed him for a second score. Last season, the young tight end really came on in the second half, finishing the campaign with six touchdown receptions. He’s only picked up one in 2026, and New England has allowed just one receiving score to the position this season. Still, Loveland’s role is growing with 21 targets over the last three games. He’s a solid bet at this price after his best game of the season. D’Andre Swift has a ton of carries for the Bears this season, handling 94 touches for 398 yards and six scores on the ground, but he hasn’t been super efficient since Week 1. Swift ran for 124 yards on 18 carries against Carolina in the season opener, yet he has just one other game (Week 3 against Philadelphia) where he’s picked up over 60 rushing yards. Backup Kyle Monangai (turf toe) has been banged up, but Swift still split time with Roschon Johnson in Week 6 and has played just 56.7 percent of the Bears’ snaps this season. New England is allowing just 3.9 yards per carry in the 2026 campaign, and I wouldn’t be shocked if Swift came up short of this rushing total again on Thursday. He has averaged less than four yards per carry in two of the last three weeks, putting up 58, 43 and 44 rushing yards during that stretch. Even if the volume is there for the veteran back, I think he’s a fade candidate in Week 7. Odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. That means the four-game absence will cost him at least $1 million in potential earnings, with the total increasing by another $250,000 for each extra game he misses. The incentive structure was a noteworthy aspect of Vera-Tucker's agreement when he joined the Patriots in March. away.headline: Patriots’ Trade of Ex-Drake Maye Weapon Resurfaces With Ironic Twist
away.blurb: Nearly two months after New England shipped the 24-year-old wide receiver to the Houston Texans , neither team has been getting much playing time out of the players involved in the deal. Patriots' Boutte Trade Draws Attention Amid Limited Playing Time The Texans officially ruled out Reed Blankenship with concussion and hand injuries, and Jalen Pitre was sidelined by a shoulder injury. Patriots' A.J. Brown Speaks out on Disappointing Performance in Loss to Bears Patriots' Trade of Ex-Drake Maye Weapon Resurfaces With Ironic Twist Unlock the latest Heavy on Patriots news — direct to your inbox. The New England Patriots made a notable choice by trading Kayshon Boutte during the offseason, but the move has reappeared with a twist. And that's attracted attention because both franchises are dealing with injuries at the positions they traded away. Patriots insider Doug Kyed mentioned the particular circumstances Sunday, Oct. 25, pointing to the slim opportunities for Boutte and safety Jaylen Reed . Getty HOUSTON, TEXAS – SEPTEMBER 20: Kayshon Boutte #14 of the Houston Texans reacts against Cincinnati Bengals during the first quarter of the game at NRG Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) The Patriots sent Boutte to Houston on Aug. 24 in exchange for Reed and a 2028 seventh-round draft pick. The move initially raised questions because Boutte had developed into a productive downfield target for quarterback Drake Maye . However, his opportunities haven't increased significantly since joining the Texans. "Texans WR Kayshon Boutte has played just 5 of 26 offensive snaps so far today, per PFF's in-game charting," Kyed wrote on X during Houston's Week 7 matchup against the New York Giants . "Patriots S Jaylen Reed, who was acquired in the Boutte trade, played just 5 of 69 defensive snaps against the Bears. Meanwhile, the Patriots are down multiple key WRs, and the Texans are down two safeties." Patriots S Jaylen Reed, who was acquired in the Boutte trade, played just 5 of 69 defensive snaps against the Bears. Meanwhile, the Patriots are down multiple key WRs, and The statistics represent an interesting comparison, with Boutte playing approximately 19% of Houston's offensive snaps at the time of Kyed's report. Meanwhile, Reed was on the field for just 7% of New England's defensive snaps during Thursday's 30-24 loss to the Chicago Bears . Boutte came into Sunday's matchup with 14 receptions for 169 yards and zero touchdowns across six games, per NFL.com , a decline from his 2025 pace in New England when he recorded 33 catches for 551 yards and six touchdowns. Reed, at present, has appeared in seven games for the Patriots, registering nine total tackles and one pass breakup. The former Penn State standout has bolstered depth in New England's secondary, and contributed on special teams. But he wasn't playing on defense often versus Chicago. away.headline: Cole Kmet suffered ‘likely season-ending injury' during Bears-Patriots game: Reports
away.blurb: Chicago Bears’ star tight end Cole Kmet is believed to have suffered a serious and potentially season-ending knee injury on a fourth-quarter reception against the New England Patriots Thursday night at Soldier Field, according to reports. NFL Network and ESPN reporter Ian Rapoport said Kmet was undergoing testing Friday morning. “Until those results come back, there is no finality,” Rapoport wrote in a post on X. Kmet had caught a pass on second down from quarterback Caleb Williams with 5:34 left to go in the game, and was moving toward the first-down marker when he was hit by two Patriots defenders. Kmet immediately began grabbing his right knee on the sideline, and was tended to by trainers for the Bears. After the TV timeout, Kmet was seen being carted off the field, giving a thumbs up to Bears fans as he left the field. The game ended in a 30-24 Bears victory . When asked at Kmet’s injury status following the game, Coach Ben Johnson didn’t sound optimistic. “We’ll know more tomorrow, but I don’t think it looked very good,” he said. Kmet has been a key reserve player for the Bears this season, serving as a mentor to Colston Loveland and still playing significant snaps for Chicago during the season. If Kmet misses any time, rookie Sam Roush would likely see more action on offense. Johnson was expected to address the media at 1 p.m. Friday. away.blurb: The Chicago Bears return to Soldier Field for their first home game since legendary coach Mike Ditka passed away, and fans in attendance against the New England Patriots are in for something special. The Hall of Fame tight end and former head coach died on Oct. 9 at the age of 86 . Ditka remains one of the most important figures in Bears history and in NFL history , and the organization is going all out to celebrate him in front of a primetime audience at Soldier Field. The Chicago Bears host the New England Patriots on Thursday Night Football in one of the most anticipated games of the 2026 NFL season, and it doubles as the team’s first home game since the passing of legendary former Bears coach Mike Ditka. Ditka led Chicago to a Super Bowl title over the Patriots following the 1985 season, which makes this matchup a fitting stage to honor him. Chicago Bears plan a stadium-wide tribute to honor Mike Ditka The Bears already honored Ditka with No. 89 jersey patches last week on the road against the Atlanta Falcons. Chicago will continue wearing the for the rest of the season in his honor. Now that the team is back home, fans get a chance to be a part of the tribute. The Bears will hold a stadium-wide mustache giveaway on Thursday night, a nod to the iconic mustache Ditka always wore. On top of that, the first 10,000 fans getting into Soldier Field will receive a Bears knit headband inspired by Ditka’s trademark sweater vest. The tribute extends to the field itself. Fans will see a commemorative Ditka stencil on the Soldier Field grass, and there will be a moment of silence held before the national anthem. The Bears also have an on-field recognition planned, along with other moments honoring the legendary coach, including a special tribute, throughout the game. It’s a great way to honor Ditka while getting the fans involved in what’s already shaping up to be a special night. home.headline: What we learned about Caleb Williams and Chicago Bears in NFL Week 6
home.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
home.blurb: The Chicago Bears were ignited by the return of former USC Trojan Caleb Williams and teammate Kyler Gordon. Both players did not miss a beat and put together dominant performances. As a result, the Bears ' offense and defense both looked good enough to make a run at the Super Bowl. Coltson Loveland was disappointing at the start of the season. Last week, however, the return of starting quarterback Caleb Williams helped him get his confidence back. Loveland had a spectacular touchdown catch on the opening drive, and he finished with 6 catches for 65 yards. The Bears offense is at its best when Loveland is making plays. It looks like the Bears' biggest playmaker is back. The NFC conference is wide open and up for grabs. The San Francisco 49ers and the Minnesota Vikings are both undefeated, but both teams have weaknesses the Bears can exploit. When this Bears team is healthy and with the return of Kyle Monangai on offense, the Bears can beat anyone in the league. Here is what we learned about the Bears in NFL Week 6: Caleb Williams looks like a top 5 quarterback One of the biggest weaknesses of Caleb Williams' game is his accuracy and his ability to play on time. Against the Atlanta Falcons, those weaknesses looked like strengths. Caleb started the game off 24/24, not missing a beat. He finished the game with an 83.3% completion percentage. That proves Caleb Williams is one of the best quarterbacks in the league. Right now, he leads the NFL with a 72.5% completion percentage. His development in year 3 has been exciting to watch and scary for the rest of the NFL to see. Kyle Monangai is such a pivotal piece to the offense Without Kyle Monangai, the Bears' run game has taken a big hit. He is the physical back that this offense needs. Without him, D'Andre Swift is a lot easier to limit. In his last game, Monangai had 30 carries for 146 yards and a touchdown. Through just 4 games, he has 324 yards and 3 touchdowns. In his absence, his true value to the offense has been on full display. It was too early to close the door on Colston Loveland When healthy Kyler Gordon is one of the best at his position in the NFL In only 16 snaps, Kyler Gordon showed he can make a massive impact. He tallied 3 sacks and a tackle for a loss on his first snap of the season. Dennis Allen is able to get extremely creative when Kyler Gordon is on the field. Gordon could be the key to the Bears' defense going from good to great. Bears are 2nd-best team in the NFC when healthy Contact/Follow @TrojansWire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of USC Trojans news, notes and opinion. Those numbers are dragged down quite a bit by the team's poor outing against the New England Patriots in Week 2, however, during which they scored just three points with 235 yards of offense. Under Mike McCarthy, the Steelers have proven that they're at least capable of explosive offensive performances. For example, they scored 30 points with 411 yards in a Week 3 victory over the Cincinnati Bengals and put up 34 points in a Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts. It's possible that Pittsburgh comes out a bit sluggish against the Saints in Paris after arriving later in the week, but the formula is there for the black and gold to have another huge performance. The Saints have struggled to consistently get after the quarterback too, as their 33.2 percent pressure rate (per SumerSports ) is the fourth-worst in the NFL despite having 15 sacks. The Steelers' offense already had their way with one of the worst defenses in the league in the Colts, and there's no reason they can't do the same vs. New Orleans by finishing with over 400 yards of total offense. Pittsburgh Forces Two Turnovers The Saints' offense cannot be taken lightly. Even though first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson has yet to play this season with a hamstring injury, while franchise left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. has been out since Week 3 after undergoing ankle surgery, they are still averaging the 11th-most points (25.3) in the league. At the same time, quarterback Tyler Shough has thrown five interceptions and lost three fumbles while New Orleans as a whole has turned the ball over 12 times , which is tied for the third-most in the NFL. Pittsburgh, meanwhile, has 10 takeaways on the year, which is tied with five other teams for the second-most behind the Green Bay Packers and Seattle Seahawks at 11. The Steelers' defense is among the better units in the league, as they allow the sixth-lowest EPA per play (-0.1) and the seventh-fewest yards per game (307.5). New Orleans is capable of doing a little bit of damage, but Pittsburgh's defense has stepped up and largely made the necessary plays when it's needed to. Winning the turnover margin is always crucial, and considering how susceptible the Saints are to giving the ball away, the Steelers will end up with two takeaways in this one. Mandatory Credit: Morgan Tencza-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Steelers Win by Two Scores Steelers Win by Two Scores Pittsburgh is short-handed along the interior of its defensive line with Sebastian Joseph-Day (triceps) joining Derrick Harmon (foot) on the reserve/injured list. The same can be said at wide receiver, as Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) are on IR as well while Ben Skowronek (calf) will miss his second-straight game . Cornerback Brandin Echols (hamstring) will be sidelined too, and there are also some questions about Rico Dowdle's (knee) availability after he was deemed questionable to suit up on the Steelers' final injury report of the week. Still, this is a game the Steelers should win. Again, maybe they aren't at tip-top shape playing overseas, but they're simply the better and more talented team. The Saints are not a pushover by any means and have the potential to make things tough for Pittsburgh, as evidenced by their comeback win over the Baltimore Ravens on the road in Week 2. That being said, New Orleans is 2-4 for a reason. Its defense is among the worst in the league, and while its offense is a formidable unit, it's going to have a tough time keeping up with the Steelers. After notching their first two-score win of the season in Week 5 vs. Indianapolis, who profiles similarly to the Saints, Pittsburgh will do so once again in France and move to 5-2. Philadelphia Eagles star quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to be done for the season after being diagnosed with blood clots in both his lungs and deep vein thrombosis. Now, with Hurts done for the year, the Eagles are being linked to a trade for a Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback. In a recent article for Bleacher Report , Kristopher Knox named the Eagles as a potential suitor for Steelers quarterback Mason Rudolph. "Mason Rudolph remains the most logical trade target for teams seeking a backup quarterback or spot starter midseason. He's one of three reserve QBs that the Pittsburgh Steelers have behind Aaron Rodgers, along with Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar," Knox wrote. "Potential Suitors : Miami Dolphins, Philadelphia Eagles." Rudolph is currently in his seventh NFL season and sixth with the Steelers. In 36 career NFL games split between the Steelers and Tennessee Titans, he has thrown 30 touchdowns, 22 interceptions, 4,925 passing yards, and has completed 64.3% of his passes. He has primarily been a backup quarterback during his career and could be a solid player for the Eagles to add to their group ahead of the deadline.

Atlanta is searching for its first home win of the season, but San Francisco presents a major test for a team still trying to find consistency on both sides of the ball. Despite the 49ers dealing with injuries, the Falcons will need a complete performance to pull off the upset. Here is how our staff sees Sunday’s matchup playing out. Garrett Chapman (3-3) The Falcons are winless at home this season, and they will need to pass a difficult test Sunday to change that trend. The undefeated 49ers have established themselves as one of the league’s top teams, and Atlanta enters the matchup with defensive holes to fill and an offense still searching for consistency. If Michael Penix Jr. can stay clean in the pocket, the Falcons will have a legitimate chance to compete. However, slowing down George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey will be especially difficult without linebacker Divine Deablo. San Francisco’s offensive weapons could prove too much for Atlanta’s defense, leading to another disappointing home result for the Falcons. Prediction : 49ers 28, Falcons 17 Scott Kennedy (3-3): At first glance, the betting line makes this matchup appear favorable for Atlanta. A 6-0 San Francisco team might be expected to be a bigger favorite, but the 49ers’ extensive injury concerns could be keeping the matchup closer than anticipated. The Falcons have enough talent to beat any team when they put everything together. The problem is finding that consistency against quality opponents. Atlanta must figure out how to handle opposing pressure, or the 49ers could overwhelm Penix with aggressive blitz packages. San Francisco is vulnerable because of its injuries, giving Atlanta a puncher’s chance. However, until the Falcons prove they can consistently perform against strong competition, picking them to pull off an upset remains difficult. Prediction : 49ers 31, Falcons 23 Darius Hayes (3-3): After Bears fans took over Mercedes-Benz Stadium last week, I expect another takeover from 49ers fans on Sunday. Atlanta should deliver a much better performance, but I still have concerns about whether the offense can do enough to secure a victory. San Francisco’s injuries will have an impact, but Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey will ultimately be too much for Atlanta’s defense. Meanwhile, the 49ers’ pass rush could make life difficult for Penix, particularly if the Falcons struggle to protect their young quarterback. I expect Atlanta to keep the game competitive and give its home crowd something to cheer about. However, until the Falcons demonstrate they can finish against a quality opponent, I cannot pick them to get over the hump. San Francisco escapes with a narrow victory, leaving Atlanta with another frustrating home loss. Prediction : 49ers 28, Falcons 24 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast (3-3) The 49ers are currently the best team in football in my opinion which makes this a tough matchup for the Falcons. This would be a lopsided matchup if the 49ers were healthy, but that’s not the case. The 49ers have been led by arguably the best passing attack in the league, but they’ll be without Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel . Stopping Georgie Kittle and McCaffrey will still be a tall order, however. The Falcons offense matches up well against the 49ers defense on paper, especially given that Nick Bosa will be out. The key will be can the Falcons o-line deal with all of the twists and stunts that the 49ers will throw at them, and can they keep Fred Warner from taking over the game. I have the 49ers winning, but I think the Falcons will keep it close. Prediction: 49ers 27, Falcons 20 Gerald Thomas, III (3-3) These are the kind of games the Falcons win. But after the last two weeks, it’s hard to pick them. This Atlanta team is still a work in progress, more than we assumed during the two-game winning streak, and the 49ers are a well-oiled machine. The skid continues. picks.blurb: Recently Cut Atlanta Falcons 3rd-Round Pick Puts Raheem Morris, 49ers on Alert Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Former Atlanta Falcons edge rusher Bralen Trice is exploring his next opportunity after visiting the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday, less than a week after appearing on Atlanta's active roster. The 49ers hosted Trice for a visit after the Falcons released him on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The former third-round pick is looking for a new home after finally making his NFL regular-season debut in 2026, following two injury-plagued seasons in Atlanta. San Francisco's defensive staff includes former Falcons head coach Raheem Morris, now the 49ers' defensive coordinator. Although Morris coached Atlanta in 2024 and 2025, Trice never played under him in a regular-season game. Trice spent his first two NFL seasons sidelined by injuries while Morris led the Falcons. If Trice joins the 49ers, he would be the second former Falcon Morris has brought to San Francisco. The 49ers signed edge rusher Khalid Kareem from the Falcons' Practice Squad before the season opener. Atlanta selected Trice with the 74th overall pick in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Washington, hoping he could develop into a productive pass rusher. However, his professional career got off to a difficult start when he tore his ACL during his first preseason game as a rookie. Trice missed the entire 2024 season before suffering another setback with the same knee during the 2025 campaign. Those injuries kept him out of a regular-season game during his first two years with the organization. The 25-year-old entered training camp healthy in 2026 but did not make Atlanta's initial 53-man roster. After clearing waivers, he returned to the Falcons' practice squad in early September. Atlanta gave Trice three weeks of practice squad elevations to prove himself. His Week 3 performance against the Green Bay Packers stood out, as he recorded four quarterback hurries while helping Atlanta's defensive front generate pressure. The Falcons eventually signed Trice to their active roster on Oct. 17 after using all three of his standard practice squad elevations. However, his time back on the 53-man roster was brief, as Atlanta released him three days later after the Falcons signed Charles Snowden from the Washington Commanders Practice Squad . Trice appeared in four games for Atlanta this season, recording two total tackles and one pass defended, according to the Falcons' official release announcement and NFL statistics. He also showed flashes as a pass rusher, particularly with his four quarterback hurries against Green Bay. For San Francisco, the visit offers a chance to evaluate a young defender who has faced significant adversity but is finally getting meaningful NFL playing time. His experience working along the defensive front could give the 49ers another option as they assess their depth at linebacker and edge defender. Morris' presence adds an interesting connection between Trice's former team and his potential next destination, even without a previous on-field relationship between the two. Trice has yet to establish himself as a consistent NFL contributor, but his healthy return in 2026 gave him his first chance to show the ability that earned him a third-round selection. Whether that opportunity continues in San Francisco remains to be seen. home.blurb: 49ers injury report: Kyle Shanahan says San Francisco may not have enough available players to reach 48 for Week 7 vs. Falcons. Shanahan said he did not think he had ever faced a situation like this in his coaching career, calling it a unique situation. For a team trying to stay unbeaten on the trip to Atlanta, the concern is not just who will be unavailable, but whether the 49ers can even fill out a full game-day roster. Which players are out for Week 7? According to Shanahan, Mike Evans, Nick Bosa, Ricky Pearsall, Deebo Samuel Sr., De’Zhaun Stribling, Demarcus Robinson, Marques Sigle, Garret Wallow and Luke Gifford were unavailable or ruled out on Sunday. Christian Kirk was in line to make his season debut, but the overall health picture still left the roster in a difficult spot. The Bosa situation was particularly notable because Shanahan said the pass rusher had worked out after previously saying he might be able to return for Week 5 or Week 6. Shanahan said Bosa was a little sore the next day, which surprised the team and did not help the outlook for this week, especially with turf coming into play. Being short on available players is one thing. Being short enough to potentially miss the 48-man threshold is another. NFL teams can elevate players from the practice squad when injuries create depth problems, and that kind of move could become important for the 49ers if the injury list keeps growing. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Won't: Browns get young playmakers going Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going. Tennessee's defense needs to set the tone early. I just don't like their odds to overcome that two weeks in a row, even if this game is in Nashville. Prediction: Titans win, 17-14 However, I don't believe the Titans will have to worry about that. Aside from their records, these two teams are oddly similar. Their defenses tend to carry them and keep games close, while their offenses tend to struggle, particularly early on in games. Cleveland is well-equipped to win those slog-style games, but will they slip up in the Music City? Here are our predictions for Week 7. Anthony Moeglin It's a Cleveland Browns party on Broadway this weekend in Nashville, Tennessee. The Browns come into this game as the favorite for the first time all season and probably the last time all season. They have a chance to get to 5-2 on the year and stay in first place. away.headline: Browns injuries: Mason Graham, OLman go out in 2nd half, Week 7 versus Titans
away.blurb: A competitive contest between the Cleveland Browns and Tennessee Titans started out as anything but in Week 7. The Titans took a 14-0 lead and looked like they would pull to 21-7 due to turnovers, but the Browns defense stepped up after a replay called back a Tony Pollard touchdown. Late in the third quarter, the team announced that Howard was questionable to return due to a concussion. We will keep you up to date on Howard’s condition as information becomes available. Cleveland ran the score to 17-14 going into halftime, helped by CB Denzel Ward’s interception and solid offensive production. On the Browns first offensive possession of the third quarter, the team was able to put together a drive that crossed midfield. Unfortunately, right tackle Tytus Howard was injured during the drive and was helped off the field, replaced by veteran Dawand Jones for the rest of the initial second-half possession. Howard limped into the blue tent on Cleveland’s sideline, with no immediate word on his condition from the team. On the next drive, Howard was seen walking to the locker room. Jones was the Browns’ fourth-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft, but has ended each of his first three seasons with injuries. Early in the fourth quarter, DT Mason Graham stayed down on the field and was seen limping off. Graham, returning after missing a few weeks due to a knee issue, looked to be in pain as he left the field. Thankfully, Graham returned a few plays later, but S Grant Delpit was removed by the officials after helping make a tackle. Delpit returned on the next Titans possession.

away.headline: Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return
away.blurb: Browns Pro Bowler Lands on Injury Report as Key Contributors Return Skip to main content SI.COM The Cleveland Browns seem to be on the mend when the injury report for Sunday’s game against the Tennessee Titans came out. Key contributors are back on the field, but they are still not out of the weeds yet, with one surprising player listed as questionable who can influence the outcome in Nashville. Denzel Ward was listed as questionable with a hand injury on Friday’s report. He was limited at practice on Friday, and the defense needs him to be healthy. Ward is having an incredible season locking down the offense’s top receiver. Another concerning, questionable designation is Quincy Williams with a neck injury. He has been flying around the field in recent weeks, making big hits and causing fumbles. Williams will be key to rushing Cameron Ward and forcing him to make bad decisions leading to errant throws and turnovers. However, Carson Schwesinger is in the lineup and he is so good that he can make up for Williams’ absence should he be out for the game. The defense continues to be hobbled as Grant Delpit is also listed as questionable with a concussion. He left last week’s game early with the injury, but has not been ruled for this week. The Browns’ stagnant rushing game will get a boost as Dylan Sampson has been upgraded to questionable. He suffered an injury in the first game of the season and has been out since. The defensive line gets a major boost with the return of Mason Graham. His injury in Week 4 looked bad, but he avoided the worst-case scenario and is back in the lineup after missing two games. Michael Hall Jr., Kalia Davis, Out Graham will need to be good, as Michael Hall Jr. continues to remain on the injured list and is out again with an ankle injury. Also on the defensive line, Kalia Davis will not play in the game. The defensive line has caused havoc for other quarterbacks and has shut down the running game. Dillon Gabriel, Teven Jenkins, Out Also out is Dillon Gabriel and Teven Jenkins. Gabriel has practiced and the Browns will have to make a decision on his injury designation soon or risk shutting him down for the season. Jenkins is out, but rookie Austin Barber has stepped up and has played well for the offensive line. If a couple of the questionable players can strap it up on Sunday, then the Browns will receive a major boost to help them improve to an AFC North best 5-2. The Titans do not have much to offer on offense, but rookie Carnell Tate is having a solid season with 344 yards, which is only one yard behind Denzel Boston. Todd Monken believes that Ward will play with a finger injury, but advised, “We’ll see”. When Ward is on the field, quarterbacks generally do not even try to throw his way, but quarterback Cameron Ward can be reckless with the football and throw it his way, leading to a crucial turnover. picks.blurb: Colts vs. Vikings | Predictions & Picks - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football U.S. Grand Prix | Live updates NFL Week 7 updates CFB Winners and Losers Rodgers makes history Top 50 MLB free agents Colts vs. Vikings | Predictions & Picks (Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images) Jake Arthur Sun, October 25, 2026 at 1:12 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads There's usually a clear path to victory for the Indianapolis Colts, even when they aren't playing well, regardless of the opponent. However, they do not match up well with the Minnesota Vikings this Sunday. The Indianapolis Colts (2-4) will attempt to ground themselves on Sunday as they travel to Minneapolis to face the host Minnesota Vikings (5-0) before their season truly spirals out of control. The Colts' 2026 campaign is at a crossroads. After consecutive losses, including an embarrassing finish last week to the previously winless Tennessee Titans , the Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard . Will that move spark the Colts and help them turn the tide, or will the team retreat into its shell? Trade rumors and thoughts of a slide are once again surrounding the Colts. This game could be a back-breaker unless they can avoid it. Here is how the ColtsRoundtable staff sees Sunday's game unfolding. Jake Arthur ( @JakeArthurNFL ): Vikings 23, Colts 13 "I'd often like to lead with the optimistic take on the matchup with a clear advantage the Colts have over their opponent, but I'm not sure there is one this week. Minnesota's defense blitzes far more than any other team, which is something the Colts' offense struggles against. The Colts can usually run the ball, but opponents are running against Minnesota less than anyone else because of the defensive fronts the Vikings present. The Vikings' offense isn't doing well despite having Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, and T.J. Hockenson, but they've had a week to figure out what to do, coming off their bye. "The Colts would often have the edge on special teams and penalties, but Minnesota's special teams are just as good as Indy's, if not better, and the Colts and Vikings are tied for being the second-least-penalized teams in the NFL. No Tyler Warren or Sauce Gardner for the Colts, and Minnesota doesn't have a soul on the injury report. The Vikings have the clear advantages in this one." Jake on the season: 2-4 Zach Hicks ( @ZachHicks2 ): Vikings 19, Colts 9 "The Colts limp into Minnesota coming off of their most embarrassing loss since 2024. They are without two of their best players in Warren and Gardner, while the 5-0 Vikings are looking healthy coming out of their bye week. The Vikings are 6.5-point favorites over the Colts on the spread, with the total set at over/under 41.5 points. Head coach Shane Steichen is now on the hot seat, while Daniel Jones has looked rusty in his return from a 2025 Achilles tear. To make matters worse, rumors are swirling that Indianapolis could move on from superstar running back Jonathan Taylor ahead of the trade deadline. Despite not having a first-round pick, a rebuild seems increasingly inevitable. The Colts' schedule doesn't get any easier over the next two weeks, with back-to-back road games against Minnesota and Jacksonville. Perhaps most notably ahead of today's matchup, cornerback Sauce Gardner and tight end Tyler Warren have both been ruled out. Warren will miss his second consecutive game, leaving Indianapolis without its top red-zone receiving threat. He also leads the Colts with 30 receptions, making his absence even more significant. I'd expect Indianapolis to lean heavily on 13 personnel, using every available weapon to get the most out of Taylor. Opposing defenses have adjusted to the Colts offense, which has struggled mightily through the air. Jones is averaging just 215 passing yards per game, and no Colts receiver has eclipsed 300 receiving yards on the season. Michael Pittman Jr. departed for Pittsburgh in the offseason, while Alec Pierce suffered another long-term injury early in the year. That has left Indianapolis with a depleted and underwhelming receiving corps featuring Josh Downs , Keenan Allen , and Laquon Treadwell. As mentioned earlier, defenses have focused on limiting Indianapolis' explosiveness on the ground. That approach has contributed to Taylor averaging a career-low 4.0 yards per carry. Gardner's absence will also loom large for a Colts defense that ranks among the league's worst, allowing 27.3 points per game, the sixth-most in the NFL. Indianapolis is also in the bottom 10 in total defense, surrendering 351.2 yards per game. It'll be fascinating to see which side comes out on top Sunday when a stoppable force (the Vikings ' offense) meets a movable object (the Colts' defense). Minnesota Vikings Preview: Key Offensive Contributors Returning Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores has been one of the biggest talking points around the NFL this season. Despite ranking in the bottom five in offensive EPA per play, Minnesota's aggressive defense has been nothing short of elite. The Vikings rank first in defensive EPA per play, allowing the second-fewest yards (259.8) and the fewest points (12.8) per game. It's the primary reason they've raced out to a sparkling 5-0 start. Flores has blitzed on more than 70% of defensive snaps this season, leaving opposing quarterbacks scrambling for answers. That pressure should be a major problem for Daniel Jones given his struggles through the air. As mentioned above, Minnesota's offense has had its own issues, but injuries have played a significant role. Kyler Murray missed 1.5 games after suffering a concussion in Week 1, while Jordan Mason landed on injured reserve. Justin Jefferson (ankle) and T.J. Hockenson (concussion) have also missed time. The good news for Minnesota is that Murray could have his usual supporting cast available Sunday. Hockenson has returned to practice following the bye, as has Mason. We've yet to see the Vikings offense at full strength, yet Minnesota remains undefeated and enters this matchup well-rested after its bye week. With key contributors potentially returning, this could finally be the game where Murray and the offense find their rhythm. Mallory drew six targets, hauling in two catches for 20 yards. From a volume perspective, Mallory should remain involved with Warren sidelined. The Miami product also posted a career-high 31% air-yard share, a promising sign for his receiving upside. His prop line has climbed in recent days, but I still think there's value at the current number. Justin Jefferson Anytime Touchdown The other play I like is Justin Jefferson to score a touchdown. Factor in Sauce Gardner's absence, and the Colts pass defense could be in for a long afternoon. Jefferson has scored a touchdown in half of his games played this season and leads all receivers with four red-zone targets. In a matchup where Minnesota should be able to move the ball against Indianapolis, I like grabbing the plus money on Jefferson to find the end zone and help lead the Vikings to their sixth consecutive win. away.headline: Vikings Make U-Turn With Running Back Before Colts Game
away.blurb: With Mason back, the Vikings will have a full complement of running backs available against the Colts. Mason will serve as an RB2 and perhaps even split carries with veteran starter Aaron Jones Sr. Vikings Make U-Turn With Running Back Before Colts Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Vikings Make U-Turn With Running Back Before Colts Game Kevin O'Connell and the Minnesota Vikings brought back running back DeeJay Dallas on the practice squad and elevated him for the Week 7 matchup versus the Indianapolis Colts. Getty Dave Holcomb Sun, October 25, 2026 at 2:40 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Running back DeeJay Dallas will play for the Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. Getty Just one day after releasing running back DeeJay Dallas, the Minnesota Vikings brought back the veteran. He will play in Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts. According to the NFL transaction wire, the Vikings signed Dallas to their practice squad Saturday. The team then elevated him to the active roster for the Week 7 matchup versus the Colts. The Vikings also announced the round of transactions with Dallas. Minnesota released Dallas from the active roster Friday to create space on the active roster for fellow running back Jordan Mason. On Saturday, the Vikings also activated Mason from injured reserve to the roster. Both running backs will play against the Colts. "To make room for Mason, the Vikings released running back DeeJay Dallas," wrote Vikings.com's Craig Peters . "Minnesota then signed Dallas to its practice squad. The veteran first joined Minnesota's practice squad in September and was signed to the 53-man roster after Mason's injury." To have space for Dallas on the practice squad, Minnesota released cornerback Natrone Brooks . Vikings Bring Back DeeJay Dallas, Elevate RB to Active Roster for Week 7 GettyRunning back DeeJay Dallas will play for the Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. Mason left in Week 1 with a fractured thumb. Needing surgery, he landed on injured reserve and missed the next four games. Week 7 was the earliest he could come off IR. In his first season with the Vikings last year, Mason had 758 rushing yards with six touchdowns. He had 59 yards and a score before leaving against the Green Bay Packers in the season opener. In his absence, Jones has carried the Vikings backfield with 410 rushing yards and two scores. He's also caught 12 passes for an additional 72 yards. Dallas only had three rushing attempts with Mason not in the lineup. He played every week but lined up for only 40 offensive snaps while receiving 92 snaps on special teams. Against the Colts, Dallas will provide extra depth behind Jones and Mason while likely focusing on special teams. The Vikings could also have rookie Demond Claiborne active for the matchup. away.blurb: Colts elevate LB Germaine Pratt, CB Kenneth Harris from practice squad to active roster; release P Thomas Morstead from practice squad Skip to main content Primary nav SCHEDULE The roster moves were made Saturday. The Indianapolis Colts today elevated cornerback Kenneth Harris and linebacker Germaine Pratt to the active roster from the practice squad for Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings. The team also released punter Thomas Morstead from the practice squad. Harris , 6-0, 192 pounds, was elevated in Week 1 vs. Baltimore and registered one solo tackle. He was signed to the team's practice squad on August 31, 2026. Harris participated in training camp with the Colts after originally signing with the team as a free agent on August 26, 2026. He previously participated in the New England Patriots' 2026 offseason program and training camp. Harris was originally signed by the Patriots as an undrafted free agent on May 8, 2026. Collegiately, he played in 59 career games (29 starts) at Oklahoma State (2023-25) and Arkansas State (2020-22) and compiled 113 tackles (92 solo), 61.5 tackles for loss, 1.0 sack, 28 passes defensed and three interceptions. Pratt , 6-3, 250 pounds, was signed to the team's practice squad on October 13, 2026. He has started 104-of-112 career games in his time with the Colts (2025-26), Las Vegas Raiders (2025) and Cincinnati Bengals (2019-24) and has totaled 734 tackles (416 solo), 38.0 tackles for loss, 3.5 sacks, 33 passes defensed, eight interceptions, eight forced fumbles, seven fumble recoveries and eight special teams stops. Pratt has started seven postseason contests and has compiled 49 tackles (32 solo), 1.0 tackle for loss, four passes defensed and one interception. In 2025, he started 12 games with Indianapolis and registered 101 tackles (57 solo), 5.0 tackles for loss, eight passes defensed, one interception, one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries. Pratt began last season with the Raiders, where he started four games and recorded 25 tackles (10 solo), 1.0 tackle for loss and two passes defensed. Morstead , 6-4, 225 pounds, was signed to the team's practice squad on October 20, 2026. He has played in 272 career games in his time with the Colts (2026), San Francisco 49ers (2025), New York Jets (2023-24, 2021), Miami Dolphins (2022), Atlanta Falcons (2021) and New Orleans Saints (2009-20). Morstead has registered 1,004 punts for 46,863 yards (46.7 avg./41.3 net avg.) with 374 pinned inside the 20-yard line. He has also totaled 263 touchbacks on kickoffs. Morstead has appeared in 18 postseason contests and has compiled 64 punts for 2,821 yards (44.1 avg./40.8 net avg.) with 22 pinned inside the 20-yard line. Getty Dave Holcomb Sun, October 25, 2026 at 2:40 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Running back DeeJay Dallas will play for the Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. Getty Just one day after releasing running back DeeJay Dallas, the Minnesota Vikings brought back the veteran. He will play in Sunday's game against the Indianapolis Colts. According to the NFL transaction wire, the Vikings signed Dallas to their practice squad Saturday. The team then elevated him to the active roster for the Week 7 matchup versus the Colts. The Vikings also announced the round of transactions with Dallas. Minnesota released Dallas from the active roster Friday to create space on the active roster for fellow running back Jordan Mason. On Saturday, the Vikings also activated Mason from injured reserve to the roster. Both running backs will play against the Colts. "To make room for Mason, the Vikings released running back DeeJay Dallas," wrote Vikings.com's Craig Peters . "Minnesota then signed Dallas to its practice squad. The veteran first joined Minnesota's practice squad in September and was signed to the 53-man roster after Mason's injury." To have space for Dallas on the practice squad, Minnesota released cornerback Natrone Brooks . Vikings Bring Back DeeJay Dallas, Elevate RB to Active Roster for Week 7 GettyRunning back DeeJay Dallas will play for the Minnesota Vikings in Week 7. Mason left in Week 1 with a fractured thumb. Needing surgery, he landed on injured reserve and missed the next four games. Week 7 was the earliest he could come off IR. In his first season with the Vikings last year, Mason had 758 rushing yards with six touchdowns. He had 59 yards and a score before leaving against the Green Bay Packers in the season opener. In his absence, Jones has carried the Vikings backfield with 410 rushing yards and two scores. He's also caught 12 passes for an additional 72 yards. Dallas only had three rushing attempts with Mason not in the lineup. He played every week but lined up for only 40 offensive snaps while receiving 92 snaps on special teams. Against the Colts, Dallas will provide extra depth behind Jones and Mason while likely focusing on special teams. The Vikings could also have rookie Demond Claiborne active for the matchup. Both teams are looking to keep their seasons from going completely off the rails, so let’s make some predictions for this Week 7 matchup. THREE BOLD PREDICTIONS Malik Washington Sets a Season High in Receiving Yards Sunday will mark the return of rookie receiver Caleb Douglas, who has missed the past three games with an ankle injury. Adding his size to the top of the depth chart should bump everyone else to a more natural position, and there may be no bigger benefactor than Malik Washington. Washington has quietly put together an impressive third season, tallying 50 or more scrimmage yards in four of his first five games. He has also established himself as a favorite target of quarterback Malik Willis, who has thrown his way 36 times this year (more than double the second-place mark). As Miami looks for sustainability, targeting Washington underneath seems like a potential solution, and he has the agility to make defenders miss in space. His ascension, Douglas’ return, and Willis likely needing quick answers against a Jets defense that ranks eighth in blitz percentage is a recipe for a big day for Miami’s most experienced receiver. Both Quarterbacks are Sacked 3+ Times This matchup features two passers who have done a poor job mitigating pressure this season. Both rank top 12 in time to throw, top three in pressure rate allowed, and top five in sack percentage. The Jets are well equipped to take advantage of Malik Willis’ indecision. Their defense ranks in the top eight in pressure rate, and is tied for sixth in total sacks through six weeks. The Dolphins, on the other hand, have been inept up front. Their four sacks are half the next-lowest team in the NFL, and all four came against Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings in Week 4. With two weeks to prepare, a quarterback who is willing to hang in the pocket, and the potentially dumb luck that Miami’s sacks have come in a bunch, this feels like a perfect opportunity for the Dolphins’ defensive front to make its mark, even if Malik Willis’ play leads to a similar outcome on the opposite side of the ball. Ollie Gordon Makes a Game-Changing Explosive Run Ollie Gordon's development in year two has been a revelation. His footwork looks substantially better than it did in 2025, and he’s made the most of his elevated opportunity. Gordon’s rushing yards over expected per attempt is ninth among qualified rushers, per NextGenStats. The Jets have a very sound defense on a per-run basis. Their EPA per rush allowed is tied for third best in football, and they’re right around the middle of the pack in terms of yards-per-attempt. They have, however, struggled to stop runs in the backfield. Their stuffed run rate is seventh-lowest, and they’re allowing over a yard and a half before contact per carry, which ranks ninth-worst. Miami’s massive offensive line has opened up big lanes for Gordon in recent weeks. He has a 20+ yard carry in each of the last two games. Now, against a defense that particularly struggles to generate displacement, it wouldn’t be shocking to see the left-side duo of Paul and Proctor give Gordon a runway that he can use to get downhill and put his massive frame to work against New York’s defensive backs. away.headline: Dolphins' Jeff Hafley returns to New Jersey seeking first Miami win
away.blurb: Coach Jeff Hafley hopes to get his first NFL head-coaching win in his home state of New Jersey. Players have identified key areas for improvement, including reducing turnovers and penalties. MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley likes to say it's about the team and not about him, but he sure would like to have his first NFL head-coaching win take place in his home state of New Jersey. "My mom will be there," Hafley said of a Week 7 game at the New York Jets . "I'll have a lot of people there. My brother, my sister, I'll probably have 30-plus people at the game. For all of us, I think it's always nice to go back close to home." Hafley hails from Montvale, N.J., only 17 miles from MetLife Stadium where Sunday's game will be played. The Dolphins are 0-5 but entered the week only 4.5-point underdogs at the Jets , who are 2-4. Miami's first five opponents were NFL playoff contenders. The Jets likely are not. And here is more good news: the Dolphins are coming off of an early bye week. "New energy, man," said Dolphins linebacker Jordyn Brooks. "Just a chance to reset. Wasn't a friendly first five weeks of the season. It was tough, kind of going through that. And we still got to live with it, but I think that break gives you a chance to kind of reflect and kind of take a deep breath and I think that's what this team needed." Predictably, the Dolphins' statistical resume after five games is poor. Miami ranks better than the league average in only 8 of the top 32 essential categories sorted and ranked by the NFL. What have the Dolphins done fairly well? "Right now, we're a team that's running the ball very well, and we're playing pretty good run defense, too," Hafley said. "We're a physical team. I think we have to build on that identity and continue to grow and develop." Miami Dolphins seek development, but also a win A lot of growth, development and patience will be required. Coaches often say they use the bye week to "self-scout" in an attempt to improve in areas they may have overlooked in the day-to-day grind of a game week. "With such a small sample size, it's not huge, but a really good time to evaluate and catch your breath and sometimes when you get to step back, you can see some things clearly," Hafley said. There are many areas in which the Dolphins must improve to win a game (short-term goal) and finish better than, say, 2-15 or 3-14 this season. But here are some self-scout reflections Dolphins players have spoken about after the bye. They also released their first injury report of the week, which included 12 players. The Dolphins listed cornerback Reese Taylor (quad) as the only non-participant. Full participants included quarterback Malik Willis (right thumb), linebacker Jordyn Brooks (foot), right guard Jonah Savaiinaea (ankle), cornerback JuJu Brents (heel) and linebacker Jackson Woodard (ankle). home.headline: Dolphins’ Caleb Douglas cleared to return from ankle injury against Jets
home.blurb: Douglas suffered the ankle ailment in the Sept. 20 loss to the San Francisco 49ers. He returned to practice this week and has been limited in drills Wednesday and Thursday before Friday’s session. After linebacker Willie Gay Jr. popped up on the Thursday injury report due to illness, Hafley said he’s back in the building Friday and feeling better. Gay participated in practice and is deemed questionable to play. Jets' Breece Hall out against Dolphins; Miami without Willie Gay The Dolphins have defensive end Rob Beal Jr., who has been back at practice through his hamstring injury, doubtful. Cornerback Reese Taylor, who has hurt quadriceps, is out. Taylor, at least, was seen participating in team stretch and then running and cutting on the side of practice, but he was still deemed a non-participant in practice. Rookie safety Kyle Louis, as he returned to practice this week, appears to be a Saturday decision on whether he is activated off injured reserve with the knee issue suffered in the opener against the Raiders. Listed as questionable, he is at least in play to return. For the Jets, coach Aaron Glenn told reporters Friday running back Breece Hall will be questionable, which held true at the release of the injury report. Hafley said he expects Hall to play after the standout rusher missed three games and he's preparing as such. New York has linebacker and Miami Hurricanes alum Kiko Mauigoa (quadriceps), offensive lineman Max Mitchell (concussion), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) ruled out. Questionable, along with Hall, are running back Kene Nwangwu (knee) and offensive lineman Dylan Parham (knee). Florida & Caribbean Experiences Florida Jewish Journal Florida Jewish Journal Branded Content Paid Partner Content MIAMI GARDENS — Miami Dolphins wide receiver Caleb Douglas is cleared to play in the upcoming game against the New York Jets on Sunday. Before Friday’s practice, Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Douglas will be good to go after missing three games with an ankle injury. The team’s injury report listed Douglas free of any game status designation after he underwent a full practice session. On Friday, Douglas appeared to be moving well running routes on air and catching passes from quarterback Malik Willis . “He's made a bunch of plays in practice,” said Hafley, who noted Douglas had taken part in individual and team portions of practice before Friday. “I'm excited to see him play. He hadn't played in a while. … It brings us some extra juice.” Without him, the Miami passing offense ranks 31st among 32 teams in the league on the year. The 6-foot-4 target who led the team with 94 receiving yards in the team’s opener against the Las Vegas Raiders could provide a boost to the passing game. Hafley also said running back Jaylen Wright, who has been dealing with a nagging foot injury, will play. They can prevent that by defeating the Carolina Panthers on Sunday, but it won't be easy to win their first division matchup. The Bucs will have Baker Mayfield back in the fold after a three-game absence, but will that be enough to get a win? Our staff goes over our predictions for Sunday's matchup against the Panthers: Caleb Skinner, Writer: Panthers 27, Bucs 21 It’s been tough sledding for the Bucs, but they might just have a chance to turn things around. Division play begins this week against the Panthers, and all signs point towards Baker Mayfield being back. While I do believe things will look better, I still think the offense is way off from being able to match Carolina’s offense, which will put up points. I think the Bucs will have a chance to win the game on the final drive, but ultimately fall short once again. James Hill, Writer: Panthers 27, Bucs 20 Mayfield's return is spoiled by the Panthers in this one. I simply think that Carolina is the better-coached team right now and that Mayfield may be slow to start back up after returning from his thumb injury. Collin Haalboom, Writer: Panthers 27, Bucs 17 The Buccaneers have played so poorly this season that they’re already on the verge of switching their primary focus from postseason contention to the top pick in next year’s NFL Draft. Considering we’re not even halfway through the season, I’d consider this season to be a full-scale nightmare for any Bucs fan. So, am I picking the Buccaneers to bounce back and take down the NFC South-leading Panthers in Carolina, you ask? No. I most certainly am not. Logan Robinson, Founder: Panthers 28, Bucs 23 The Panthers head into the game with the top passing attack in the league, and Bryce Young is playing at a high caliber. The Bucs and Todd Bowles have done a fair job of defending these types of offenses this season. My biggest concern is the offense for Tampa Bay. It’s quite obvious Zac Robinson’s offense doesn’t have an identity and even with Baker Mayfield coming back, I just don’t see it changing much. They’ll have to begin proving me wrong before I pick them to win games. Also, a reminder — the Cowboys are a bad football team. River Wells, Editor: Panthers 28, Bucs 17 Tampa Bay's defense will be tested by a Panthers offense that playcaller Brad Idzik has unlocked this season. Bryce Young is stretching the football down the field in a dominant way, so expect the Panthers to score points. Don't expect the Bucs to do much on offense in return. Zac Robinson's offense has been scattershot this whole season, and while Mayfield should play better than Jalon Daniels, he'll be playing with an injured thumb after a year where he didn't start off so hot anyway. Bucs have to be able to run the ball on Carolina — if they can't, they have no chance of winning. Consensus: Panthers 5, Bucs 0 The Buccaneers still haven't given us a reason to pick them to win a football game. They're 1-5 as it stands, and every BucsGameday staff member thinks they'll be 1-6 whenever they wake up in the morning. This week, they're headed back home to take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in an early-season rivalry bout. While the Buccaneers are struggling at the bottom of the division, these matchups are always tough and important. So, what do the odds tell us this week? One could argue that the spread is a little too small given the trajectory of the two franchises and the most recent outings for both. Regardless, the Panthers are favored at home. They're -105 to cover the spread, while the Buccaneers are -115 to cover. That's also a little bit interesting. The Panthers have won three contests by an average of 16 points. The Panthers are -180 on the moneyline, so they are expected to win outright. The Buccaneers are +152 to win. The over/under is set at 44.5, and the over and under are both currently set at -110. So, based on that, the oddsmakers expect the Panthers to win a tight contest, 24-21. In other words, the Panthers are not expected to blow out a 1-5 team at home. Now, there is a huge caveat to these odds and what they're telling us. Right now, it is totally up in the air as to which QB the Panthers will see. away.headline: Buccaneers expect Baker Mayfield back, rule out three starters
away.blurb: The Buccaneers' official Friday injury report lists wide receiver Emeka Egbuka, right tackle Luke Goedeke, and safety Antoine Winfield Jr. as ruled out. Baker Mayfield remains questionable with a right thumb injury, although head coach Todd Bowles expects him to start against Carolina. Getting Mayfield back would significantly boost an offense that has struggled to establish consistency. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels has done a respectable job given his limited NFL experience, but Mayfield's ability to recognize pressure, adjust protections, and make pre-snap decisions gives offensive coordinator Zac Robinson more flexibility. However, Tampa Bay's offense will be far from full strength on Sunday. Egbuka missed Wednesday and Thursday's practices with concussion and foot injuries before returning Friday in a limited capacity. Despite the improvement, the team ruled him out for Sunday's game. His absence removes one of Tampa Bay's primary receiving threats from an offense that has already struggled to create consistent opportunities downfield. Goedeke also returned to practice in a limited capacity Friday after missing the previous two sessions with a calf injury. He was ultimately ruled out, leaving Tampa Bay without its starting right tackle. Protecting Mayfield will be especially important if he returns against a Carolina defense looking to exploit an offensive line that has struggled this season. Defensively, Winfield will miss Sunday's game with a rib injury. The veteran safety was limited all week but couldn't return to game action. His absence adds to the challenge for a young defense that has shown encouraging signs despite Tampa Bay's 1-5 record. Carolina will also deal with injuries, particularly on its defensive front. Outside linebackers Jaelan Phillips and Thomas Incoom were ruled out after missing all three practices. Offensive tackle Monroe Freeling and linebacker Bam Martin-Scott are questionable despite participating fully throughout the week. The Buccaneers enter Sunday's game looking to rebound from a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Mayfield's expected return gives Tampa Bay reason to be optimistic, but the absences of Egbuka, Goedeke, and Winfield will force the team to adjust on both sides of the ball.
