away.headline: Buccaneers crush turnover-prone Panthers 43-13 in Baker Mayfield's return
away.blurb: The Panthers couldn't get out of the way of the Buccaneers' freight train on Sunday. The Bucs led 17-0 early in the first quarter, 33-6 at halftime and blew out the Panthers 43-13. It was ugly for the home team, which turned it over four times for 20 Buccaneers points and gave up a 2-point defensive conversion on a blocked PAT. The Bucs are 2-5 and the Panthers 3-3. Baker Mayfield returned after missing three games with a broken right thumb, but the Panthers' ineptitude and the Bucs' run game powered Tampa Bay. The Bucs rushed for 258 yards on 49 carries, with three backs over 50 yards rushing. Bucky Irving led the way with 24 carries for 106 yards and two touchdowns. Kenneth Gainwell added 88 yards on 14 carries, and Sean Tucker had seven carries for 52 yards and a touchdown. Mayfield was only 7-of-11 for 64 yards and a touchdown, a 14-yard throw to Tez Johnson. Bryce Young threw two interceptions and lost a fumble on a strip-sack Al-Quadin Muhammad that Calijah Kancey returned 32 yards for a touchdown. David Moore muffed a punt that Ko Kieft recovered for the Bucs at the Carolina 18. The Bucs had scoring drives of 14, 32 and 6 in addition to their defensive touchdown. They also had the NFL's first defensive 2-point conversion of the season when Tykee Smith blocked Ryan Fitzgerald’s PAT attempt and Zyon McCollum returned it to the end zone. McCollum also had one of the picks of Young.

home.blurb: Bryce Young and the Carolina Panthers were off to a solid start this season, but had some of their weaknesses exposed against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Young struggled in the 43-13 loss to the Bucs, throwing for just 163 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions on 14-of-27 passing. Unfortunately for Young and the Panthers' offense, they got little help from the defense. While Baker Mayfield had just 64 passing yards and a touchdown in his first game back since Week 3, Tampa Bay rushed for 258 yards and three touchdowns. Bucky Irving led the charge with 106 yards and two touchdowns on 24 carries. While the Panthers came into Sunday's matchup 3-2, their run defense had been inconsistent at best. They gave up 291 yards to the Chicago Bears in Week 1 but had success against top running backs like Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs. Carolina will need to be more consistent in keeping the ground game controlled if it wants to win the division and reach the playoffs again. As for Young, he came into the matchup against the Bucs ranking inside the top 10 in passing yards, touchdowns and interceptions, continuing to build off a career season in 2025. Clearly, Tampa Bay's defense rattled him, and he looked more like the rookie version of himself.

Here are Baltimore Beatdown's last-minute predictions: Like the Falcons, the Bengals seem like an especially bad matchup for the Ravens. Baltimore's offensive line finally has their best five, but it is still Cam Jurgens' first game snapping to Tyler Huntley in a new offense. And he has to deal with Dexter Lawrence. On defense, well, we've seen this movie before Joe Burrow to Ja'Marr Chase for first down or a touchdown at all of the worst moments. But I picked against the Ravens in Atlanta, and Derrick Henr X-factor: Ja'Kobi Lane. Huntley needs a big, quarterback-friendly target that he can trust with contested catches, whether he's trying to push the ball downfield or hit a hot read against the blitz. Lane has proven he can operate in traffic over the middle with a good feel for picking up the requisite yards for a first down. This feels like a good week for his first regular-season touchdown. Score prediction: Ravens 24, Bengals 21 With no Lamar Jackson, the Ravens' offense will again be limited. Therefore, the onus will be on their defense to carry the load, as they did last week, but forcing turnovers may be necessary. If the Ravens' defense can come up with a takeaway or two and give their offense a short-field to work with, that could make a huge difference. Their pass rush against Joe Burrow needs to be relentless and effective to disrupt the Bengals' lethal passing attack. X-factor: Cam Jurgens. Expecting great results from Jurgens in his first game as a Raven, coming off a concussion, may be unfair. However, the Ravens will need him to hold his own in a tough matchup against DT Dexter Lawrence. If Jurgens is overwhelmed in one-on-one matchups with Lawrence, the latter might wreck any chance of offensive success for the Ravens. Score prediction: Ravens 17, Bengals 24 Kevin McNelis Last week wasn't pretty, and while they get multiple pieces a little healthier, they're now down Tavius Robinson and still without Lamar Jackson. It doesn't bode well as they face a well-rounded Bengals team that's given the secondary fits even when the Ravens have managed to win against them over the past few seasons. Derrick Henry's success was limited last week, and maybe the offense can mix it up a little bit more than they did last week, but they're going to need the defense to make some plays and set up short fields if they want to have any hope of winning this game. The next guys up in Zion Young, Mike Green, and Keondre Jackson filling in for Jaylinn Hawkins can prove that they deserve bigger spots by stepping up and making big plays in the expanded roles. X-factor: I'd even venture to give Keondre Jackson my X-factor player for this game based on how important the back end of the defense is going to be as they face the Bengals receivers. My heart has hope, but my head feels like it knows where this game goes. Score prediction: Bengals 27, Ravens 16 Any game without Lamar Jackson will be tough to win for the Ravens, but a divisional matchup with a Bengals team fresh off a bye week is an especially difficult hurdle to overcome with a backup quarterback. If Baltimore wants to pull off the upset with Tyler Huntley on Sunday, then getting the run game going with Derrick Henry is absolutely paramount to sustaining offensive success. Henry was bottled up against the Browns a week ago and Huntley was unable to carry the load with his arm. If the Ravens can get a classic Henry performance, then they should have a real chance against the Bengals. Baltimore's defense has played better in recent weeks, but Sunday will present their toughest challenge yet with Joe Burrow throwing to Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. The Ravens' secondary has done a good job of eliminating explosive plays down the field, but Chase and Higgins will put that to the test. I predict a respectable fight from the Ravens, but without Jackson, I do not foresee Baltimore's offense having enough juice to keep up with Cincinnati's passing attack over the course of four quarters. X-factor: Trey Hendrickson. Hendrickson is surely chomping at the bit to get back at his former team on Sunday. While the secondary will need to be at their best, an effective pass rush would go a long way in preventing Burrow from having a field day through the air. Score prediction: Bengals 27 Ravens 20

away.headline: Bengals WR Tee Higgins returns from Kyle Hamilton's hit to catch TD
away.blurb: Cincinnati Bengals receiver Tee Higgins was injured during the third quarter of the team's NFL Week 7 game against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium but returned a short time later to catch Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow's second touchdown pass of the day. Higgins' arm and shoulder were observed on the sideline by team medical personnel after taking a huge hit from Ravens defensive back Kyle Hamilton following a 10-yard catch on third down during the Bengals' second drive early in the second half. Higgins remained on the Bengals' bench after observation. He had a 19-yard catch during the Bengals' next possession, his third reception of the second half. He caught the TD from Burrow later in the same drive. Start the day smarter. Get all the news you need in your inbox each morning. Before the bye week, Higgins was dealing with an adductor injury he suffered in a Week 4 loss to Jacksonville. Against the Jaguars, Higgins got up slowly after a 19-yard catch near the sideline from quarterback Burrow . Higgins got up, but then took a knee and required attention from team medical personnel. Higgins returned to the game later in the drive, and made a catch on his first play back in the game. He was not on the field for the Bengals' final drive of the game. Higgins had a game-high 10 catches for 140 receiving yards before the injury. He added a 17-yard catch, giving him a total of 157 receiving yards, second only to the 194-yard game he had against Baltimore in 2021. Higgins made a remarkable touchdown catch from quarterback Burrow late in the second quarter of the team's Week 3 loss to Pittsburgh at Acrisure Stadium. It was among the most impressive NFL catches by Higgins . In March 2025, Higgins agreed to a four-year contract extension with the team. Higgins, Cincinnati's second-round pick in the 2020 NFL draft, is entering his seventh NFL season. The 29-year-old suffered the injury in Week 4 during the Ravens' game against the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. Ever since, Baltimore has struggled on the field in his absence, losing last week to the Cleveland Browns and narrowly escaping with a win in overtime against a shorthanded Atlanta Falcons team the Sunday before. away.blurb: Concerning Lamar Jackson Injury Update Shifts Bengals vs. Ravens Odds in NFL Week 7 Skip to main content ON SI Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has not played since Week 4, and his status for Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals still remains unclear. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson could "potentially" practice this week after missing all three of the team's practices ahead of Week 6. There have been reports the last two weeks that Jackson has a chance to play through his ankle injury, but he has not suited up in practice -- or for a game -- since Week 4. Minter: Lamar Jackson (ankle) could "potentially" practice this week. Remains day-to-day. Minter's update on Jackson isn't viewed as a positive one in the betting market. Ahead of Week 7, oddsmakers set the Ravens as three-point favorites at home in their matchup with the Bengals. Now, DraftKings Sportsbook has Baltimore set as a 2.5-point favorite, though it remains -148 on the moneyline to win this game. It's not a major adjustment, but clearly there is some worry that Jackson could miss his third game in a row. Currently, DraftKings has received 73 percent of the moneyline bets in this game on the Bengals to win outright. After going down against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4, Jackson has not played. He missed a win over Atlanta in Week 5 and a loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6. The Cleveland loss looms large for the Ravens, as they are now behind the Browns in the AFC North standings. The Ravens are a much more dangerous team with Jackson in the lineup, and he was an MVP candidate before going down in Week 4. This season, the star quarterback has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. A two-time MVP, Jackson leads the league in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating in 2026. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score, a sign that his rushing is back to a higher level than it was in 2025. Tyler Huntley would receive the start in Week 7 if Jackson can't go. Dating back to last season, the Ravens are 3-1 in Huntley's last four starts, but they remain 7-12 all-time when Jackson is sidelined. Huntley struggled to move the offense in Week 6, throwing for 165 yards and a score in a 13-10 loss. He did combine for three scores in the win over Atlanta, so there is a higher ceiling that what he showed this past Sunday. If Jackson doesn't practice on Wednesday, it's possible this line could move even further towards the Bengals. For now, oddsmakers are still giving the Ravens the edge in this divisional battle. Ever since, Baltimore has struggled on the field in his absence, losing last week to the Cleveland Browns and narrowly escaping with a win in overtime against a shorthanded Atlanta Falcons team the Sunday before. home.blurb: Concerning Lamar Jackson Injury Update Shifts Bengals vs. Ravens Odds in NFL Week 7 Skip to main content ON SI Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson has not played since Week 4, and his status for Week 7 against the Cincinnati Bengals still remains unclear. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Jackson could "potentially" practice this week after missing all three of the team's practices ahead of Week 6. There have been reports the last two weeks that Jackson has a chance to play through his ankle injury, but he has not suited up in practice -- or for a game -- since Week 4. Minter: Lamar Jackson (ankle) could "potentially" practice this week. Remains day-to-day. Minter's update on Jackson isn't viewed as a positive one in the betting market. Ahead of Week 7, oddsmakers set the Ravens as three-point favorites at home in their matchup with the Bengals. Now, DraftKings Sportsbook has Baltimore set as a 2.5-point favorite, though it remains -148 on the moneyline to win this game. It's not a major adjustment, but clearly there is some worry that Jackson could miss his third game in a row. Currently, DraftKings has received 73 percent of the moneyline bets in this game on the Bengals to win outright. After going down against the Tennessee Titans in Week 4, Jackson has not played. He missed a win over Atlanta in Week 5 and a loss to the Cleveland Browns in Week 6. The Cleveland loss looms large for the Ravens, as they are now behind the Browns in the AFC North standings. The Ravens are a much more dangerous team with Jackson in the lineup, and he was an MVP candidate before going down in Week 4. This season, the star quarterback has completed 70.8 percent of his passes for 967 yards, six scores and just one interception. A two-time MVP, Jackson leads the league in yards per attempt, yards per completion and passer rating in 2026. He also has 19 carries for 144 yards and a score, a sign that his rushing is back to a higher level than it was in 2025. Tyler Huntley would receive the start in Week 7 if Jackson can't go. Dating back to last season, the Ravens are 3-1 in Huntley's last four starts, but they remain 7-12 all-time when Jackson is sidelined. Huntley struggled to move the offense in Week 6, throwing for 165 yards and a score in a 13-10 loss. He did combine for three scores in the win over Atlanta, so there is a higher ceiling that what he showed this past Sunday. If Jackson doesn't practice on Wednesday, it's possible this line could move even further towards the Bengals. For now, oddsmakers are still giving the Ravens the edge in this divisional battle. picks.blurb: Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans, Why They Won’t, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New York Giants might have a winning record (3-2-1) right now and lead the NFC East. But let’s be honest. Aside from their dominant Week 1 showing against the Dallas Cowboys, have the Giants really looked as good as their record suggests? We’re talking about a team where the phrase “A win’s a win” applies. The Giants barely beat the Tennessee Titans, 12-7, in Week 3. They also had to fight back in Week 4 against the Arizona Cardinals, who led 24-19 at one point. The tie against the Commanders? That one was a gift. If Jayden Daniels and Dan Quinn don’t have that brain blip, the Commanders likely win, despite the Giants roaring back from a 19-6 deficit. And last week? We’re sorry, but the Giants had no business losing to the New Orleans Saints as badly as they did. And again, make no mistake: the Giants lost that game because they were their own worst enemy, as shown by the sloppy play they put on film. But it’s funny how the football gods work. The Giants, regardless of what they do against the Houston Texans this week, will remain in first place in the division. They have a chance, albeit a difficult one, to get back to looking like the team they were in Week 1, even though they’ve since lost a lot of key personnel, all of whom played in that win: quarterback Jaxson Dart, returner/receiver Braxton Berrios, outside linebacker Brian Burns, and inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds. So what’s the goal this week if the Giants want to pull off an upset win over the Texans on the road? “We’ve been practicing well the last few weeks,” head coach John Harbaugh said. “I think practice has been improving every single week, which is the mark of a team that has got a chance to do something. You’ve got to keep improving. “So, we are on track to do that. I’m looking forward to it showing up in terms of consistency. If we’ve been anything, we’ve been inconsistent.” It’s really that simple. The question is, will the Giants finally find the consistency that’s eluded them since that Week 1 game? Why the Giants Will Beat the Texans The Texans might be on a roll, having won their last two games, but they still have a few flaws that could work to the Giants’ advantage. For one, the Texans’ offensive line ranks 27th in the PFF pass-blocking efficiency rating metric. The unit has allowed 71 quarterback pressures, tied for third-most in the league. Left tackle Aireontae Ersery has allowed 20 quarterback pressures, per PFF, tied for fourth-most in the league among left tackles. Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has turned up the heat on opposing quarterbacks in recent weeks. This year, opposing quarterbacks have completed only 54.1% of their pass attempts against the Giants’ blitz, the fourth-lowest completion rate in the league. Of course, the key is for the Giants to stop the run, something they haven’t done consistently in recent weeks. So we’ll see if Wilson’s calling out his defensive players for not running to the ball lights a fire underneath them. Offensively, the Giants need to get their running game going, and the hope is that switching to quarterback J.J. McCarthy will help. This more mobile quarterback will discourage the Texans from loading up the box and start accounting for McCarthy as a runner. More importantly, McCarthy’s ability to scramble away from trouble could help the Giants’ ailing offensive tackles, Andrew Thomas and, if he plays, Jermaine Eluemunor, against that Texans pass rush. Per Next Gen Stats, since 2025, McCarthy has scrambled 19 times for 185 yards and three touchdowns, a 9.7 yards-per-carry average, which is a league high among quarterbacks with a minimum of 15 carries. If McCarthy can buy time, he stands a chance at connecting with receiver Malik Nabers or tight end Isaiah Likely, both of whom have been the most frequently targeted players on offense for the Giants over the last few weeks. Why the Giants Will Lose to the Texans I touched on it a bit above, but I’ll say it again here. The Giants have to stop the run. Texans’ top running back, David Montgomery, has been sidelined with a groin injury, but Woody Marks has stepped up in his place. Marks is an explosive running back who has averaged almost four yards per rush over the last two weeks. He also has six catches for 47 yards over that span. The Giants’ run defense? Not good at all. Big Blue has allowed opponents 135.5 rushing yards per game this year, and their 5.0 yards per carry allowed is the second-worst average in the league. If the Giants can’t stuff Marks and the Texans’ running game, it won’t matter what pass-rush plan they have this week. And until the unit shows it has cleaned up the missed tackles (13 last week, seven against the run per PFF), that aspect of the game will remain the team’s Achilles heel. At the start of the season, I had this game down as a loss and nothing — not even the Texans’ 2-4 record or the Giants’ 3-2-1 start — has changed my mind. The Texans have been coming into their own lately, and the Giants, aside from their Week 1 win over Dallas, have barely gotten by in their other wins and in their tie against Washington. The Giants will fight — that much I am certain of — and I hope this doesn’t turn into the ugly rout that I fear it could become. After a 0-4 start to the season, Houston got back on track with a 26-3 win in Tennessee, and then a 34-31 win over the Jaguars in London last week. On the other hand, the Giants haven’t won a game since starting the season 3-1. Of course, they played to a tie in Washington before falling 34-27 at home to the Saints last week. Using the latest odds and analysis, here’s where I’m leaning for this Week 7 matchup with a final score prediction. Giants vs. Texans Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Giants +10.5 (-112) Texans -10.5 (-108) 42.5 (Over -118/Under -102) Line Movement: The spread has moved an important point since the odds opened for this game, going from -9.5 to -10.5. The total has also moved by a point, going down from 43.5 to 42.5. Giants vs. Texans Final Score Prediction SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan broke down this game in his Road to 272 Bets column, in which he picks each game every week: Giants vs. Texans Prediction The No. 1 thing that immediately sticks out to me when it comes to these two teams in their difference in their strengths of schedule. Sure, the Texans may be 2-4, and the Giants are 3-2-1, but the Texans have had the sixth most difficult schedule so far this season, with games against the likes of the Bills, Bengals, Cowboys, and Jaguars. Meanwhile, the Giants have had the third-easiest schedule in the league with games against the Titans, Cardinals, Commanders, and Saints. The Houston offense continues to look like a completely different unit as long as Nico Collins remains healthy. Its defense has had a slow start, but I still have faith they'll be one of the best defenses in the NFL for the rest of the way. They'll be able to put the Giants' quarterback in a blender, no matter who it ends up being on Sunday. I don't mind laying the points on Houston. Pick: Texans -9.5 (-110) via BetRivers The Texans are clearly the better overall team than the Giants, despite their records, as MacMillan mentioned, but I think I still need to see an impressive win before I can lay double-digit points. Sure, the Texans blew out the Titans 26-3 two weeks ago, but the Giants are better than Tennessee, and New York’s only blowout loss came in a game where they lost Jaxson Dart early on. picks.blurb: Texans' Week 7 Odds Point to Potential Blowout vs. Giants, J.J. McCarthy Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Houston Texans head into their Week 7 contest against the New York Giants riding the high of logging two straight wins over their last two matchups, and now hope to extend that streak to three in their last game before the bye. And the pieces could certainly be in place for the Texans to make that third consecutive win become a reality. Their offense is looking the best it has all season after another strong performance from C.J. Stroud. The defense will have the task of facing a new starting quarterback on the other side in J.J. McCarthy , and all of that coming back on Houston's home field tends to make their chances look even better. And when looking at the Texans' betting odds heading into Week 7, it's becoming pretty clear that the sportsbooks have one obvious favorite in mind for this weekend's action in Houston. Texans Already Projected to Rout the Giants in Week 7 According to recent odds from FanDuel Sportsbook , the Texans are now listed as 10.5-point favorites (-550 ML) over the Giants in Week 7. That's by far the Texans' highest spread heading into any week they've played this season. And when looking around the league's Week 7 matchups, Houston is currently the only team listed as a favorite by more than a touchdown––let alone being a favorite by double digits. Oct 11, 2026; Nashville, Tennessee, USA; Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) celebrates his touchdown with wide receiver Nico Collins (12) against the Tennessee Titans during the second half at Nissan Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. The projected point-total for these two teams doesn't look favorable for the Giants either. Houston and New York have an over-under sitting at 43.5, which comes in tied for bottom-five among the NFL in terms of projected totals for Week 7. So if the Texans are projected to win by double-digits, and the total score isn't expected to reach above 43 points, that's not much of an optimistic statement from the books on how this Giants offense could fare against a Houston defensive unit that many considered among the best in the NFL heading into this season. Will the Texans Actually Dominate the Giants as Expected? Now, projections are one thing. Clearly, the consensus is starting to lean in one clear direction for this one between the Texans and the Giants. But does Houston actually have what it takes to make that double-digit victory come to fruition? Really, it all relies upon the defense. Last game against the Jacksonville Jaguars showed that the Texans' offense is starting to get into a bit of a rhythm . A ton of receivers are getting involved and making plays, the run game showed signs of life against one of the best rushing defenses in the NFL, and the offensive line even held up to zero sacks. But the Texans' defense just hasn't been as consistently elite as this team proved to be last year. That's not saying they can't find their way back to that level–– because the personnel looks virtually identical to last year outside of a select few changes. But we still need to see Houston have multiple strong weeks defensively to really have this level of confidence in their chances on Sunday. After all, the Giants have won three games as is this season. That's more than the Texans can claim for themselves, and New York sits atop the NFC East because of it. So as 10.5-point underdogs, they seem just a slight bit underrated here, simply when considering Houston's inconsistencies on defense. Maybe the Texans wind up crushing those projections anyways, but perhaps the Giants can make this game just a little bit more interesting than the odds tend to show. away.headline: Will New York Giants OL Jermaine Eluemunor play vs. Houston Texans?
away.blurb: However, they will be short several players. Linebacker Tremaine Edmunds has been placed on season-ending injured reserve (IR), while tight end Theo Johnson and safety Jevon Holland have been downgraded to out. Safety Tyler Nubin is likely to play despite a questionable designation, but the status of right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor remains somewhat unclear. Eluemunor left a Week 5 game against the Washington Commanders with a calf injury and was swiftly ruled out. He was listed as week-to-week, and that proved to be a fair expectation after Eluemunor was listed as inactive last Sunday against the Saints. Starting the week, Eluemunor was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice before practicing on a limited basis both Thursday and Friday. He was given a questionable designation, which was also the case in Week 6. If Eluemunor isn't able to play on Sunday, things get a bit sketchy for the Giants. Last week's go-to, second-year swing tackle Marcus Mbow, is also listed as questionable with a knee issue. Like Eluemunor, he was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice before being limited on Thursday and Friday. Should Eluemunor be listed as inactive after pregame warmups and Mbow is cleared to play, he would draw the start. If both are out, the Giants would be forced to start rookie J.C. Davis, who has largely served as Thomas' backup this season. The only other option for the Giants is Josh Sills, who was recently signed off of the Indianapolis Colts' practice squad. He has primarily played guard throughout his career, but does have limited experience at both left and right tackle. However, the fact that the Giants did not elevate another offensive lineman ahead of Sunday's game is a good indication they plan on having Eluemunor and/or Mbow available. The New York Giants will visit the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium in Houston, Texas, on Sunday afternoon in Week 7, where they will look to bounce back from a disappointing loss against the New Orleans Saints and head into their bye week on a high note. Jermaine Eluemunor injury update As of Friday afternoon, there was no clear indication that Eluemunor would or would not play against the Texans. Will Jermaine Eluemunor play vs. Texans? Eluemunor traveled with the team to Houston, and his status was not changed on Saturday when the Giants announced injury updates. That is a positive sign. "If those guys are able, and it looks like based on today's practice, that they should have a good chance to be ready to go, that will be really important," head coach John Harbaugh said of Eluemunor and Andrew Thomas on Friday. Thomas was not given an injury designation. The Giants will officially release their inactives 90 minutes before kickoff. Who would replace Jermaine Eluemunor in the lineup? away.headline: New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything
away.blurb: This will also make New York a step slower in its front seven, which will not only affect the pass rush (Edmunds actually has a couple of sacks this season), but also its pass coverage, which was already questionable. New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL New York Giants' Shocking Injury News Just Changed Everything (Sam Navarro-Imagn Images) Matthew Schmidt Sat, October 24, 2026 at 11:00 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As if the New York Giants didn't already have enough injuries, they just lost yet another key players for the year, as linebacker Tremaine Edmunds has gone down with a season-ending shoulder injury. Edmunds popped up on the injury report this week with the shoulder issue, but it didn't appear to be too big of a deal. Evidently, it was more serious than initially anticipated. Now, the Giants have lost the anchor of their linebacking corps, the man they signed to a three-year, $36 million contract in free agency back in March. New York's run defense was already struggling as it was, so to subtract Edmunds on top of that will make things that much more challenging for Big Blue. Micah McFadden will now step back into a starting role, and fortunately, he has long proven to be serviceable — but he is a definitive downgrade from Edmunds. This injury changes absolutely everything for the Giants. Edmunds' absence will now put that much more pressure on rookie Arvell Reese, and it also means that Reese's mentor will no longer be on the field with him. Reese has looked spectacular in certain moments this year, but he has also looked very much like a first-year player at other times, so losing Edmunds will unquestionably have an effect on the youngster. And of course, it will also give running backs yet even more of a chance to break through the Giants' linebacking corps and into the defensive backfield. New York has now lost two of its top defensive players in Edmunds and Brian Burns, which is beyond devastating for a unit that displayed so much potential during the season opener. The Giants are now incredibly thin on that side of the ball, and in an NFC East that is totally up for grabs, New York may slowly be losing its advantage. To make matters worse, the schedule is about to get tougher. The Giants will face the suddenly hot Houston Texans on the road on Sunday before heading into their bye week. Then, New York will begin a difficult stretch that runs all the way through Week 18. Even in such a horrendous division, it's becoming harder and harder to view the Giants as a potential playoff team given all of their injuries. First, Jaxson Dart . Then Burns. Now Edmunds. It continues to snowball.

away.blurb: Thomas, who has sat out Wednesday and Thursday over the past several weeks and returned to practice on a limited basis on Friday and Saturday before being cleared to play, is someone to watch this week. Last week he came out of the game just before the big fourth-quarter comeback attempt against the Saints; the veteran left tackle was visibly laboring through his groin injury throughout the game. Starting safety Jevon Holland was spotted at practice, off to the side with a trainer. Newsome and Holland have been the Giants defensive secondary’s best players so far this season, so hopefully their absences aren’t serious enough to keep them out of Sunday’s game. Speaking of the cornerback position, Newsome did not practice, but rookie Colton Hood (concussion) did. Sills, 6-foot-6 and 325 pounds, was originally an undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma State whom the Eagles signed in 2022. That season, Sills, who has played guard in his short NFL career, was one of three undrafted free agents to make the Eagles roster but only appeared in one game for Philadelphia. Giants Injury Report: Giants O-line Thinned By Injuries Skip to main content SI.COM The New York Giants will face one of the best defenses on Sunday when they travel to Houston to meet the Texans. So it was a bit alarming that on Wednesday, the team’s top three offensive tackles were not practicing. Starters Andrew Thomas (groin), Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and swing tackle Marcus Mbow (knee) were not participating in practice during the media viewing period. Eluemunor missed last week’s game as well with his injury after saying he would test it to see if he could anchor; he is also someone to watch this week. And with MBow now nursing something, the Giants could be thin at offensive tackle if he can’t play. The Texans have league sack leader Will Anderson, Jr. on one side of their formation and Danielle Hunter on the other. That would be quite the test for rookie J.C. Davis, who would presumably play left tackle; at right tackle, the Giants could potentially move Sisi Mauigoa from right guard to tackle, the position he played in college. Edmunds, Newsome Not Spotted During Media Viewing Portion of Practice Inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) and cornerback Greg Newsome II (concussion) were not spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. If Edmunds can’t go, Micah McFadden would get the start. The question then becomes who would wear the radio in his helmet: rookie Arvell Reese, the most likely candidate, or someone else. Rookie Colton Hood (concussion), receiver Darnell Mooney (neck), safety Tyler Nubin (neck), and tight end Theo Johnson (neck) were spotted at practice during the media viewing portion. home.headline: Will New York Giants OL Jermaine Eluemunor play vs. Houston Texans?
home.blurb: However, they will be short several players. Linebacker Tremaine Edmunds has been placed on season-ending injured reserve (IR), while tight end Theo Johnson and safety Jevon Holland have been downgraded to out. Safety Tyler Nubin is likely to play despite a questionable designation, but the status of right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor remains somewhat unclear. Eluemunor left a Week 5 game against the Washington Commanders with a calf injury and was swiftly ruled out. He was listed as week-to-week, and that proved to be a fair expectation after Eluemunor was listed as inactive last Sunday against the Saints. Starting the week, Eluemunor was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice before practicing on a limited basis both Thursday and Friday. He was given a questionable designation, which was also the case in Week 6. If Eluemunor isn't able to play on Sunday, things get a bit sketchy for the Giants. Last week's go-to, second-year swing tackle Marcus Mbow, is also listed as questionable with a knee issue. Like Eluemunor, he was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice before being limited on Thursday and Friday. Should Eluemunor be listed as inactive after pregame warmups and Mbow is cleared to play, he would draw the start. If both are out, the Giants would be forced to start rookie J.C. Davis, who has largely served as Thomas' backup this season. The only other option for the Giants is Josh Sills, who was recently signed off of the Indianapolis Colts' practice squad. He has primarily played guard throughout his career, but does have limited experience at both left and right tackle. However, the fact that the Giants did not elevate another offensive lineman ahead of Sunday's game is a good indication they plan on having Eluemunor and/or Mbow available. The New York Giants will visit the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium in Houston, Texas, on Sunday afternoon in Week 7, where they will look to bounce back from a disappointing loss against the New Orleans Saints and head into their bye week on a high note. Jermaine Eluemunor injury update As of Friday afternoon, there was no clear indication that Eluemunor would or would not play against the Texans. Will Jermaine Eluemunor play vs. Texans? Eluemunor traveled with the team to Houston, and his status was not changed on Saturday when the Giants announced injury updates. That is a positive sign. "If those guys are able, and it looks like based on today's practice, that they should have a good chance to be ready to go, that will be really important," head coach John Harbaugh said of Eluemunor and Andrew Thomas on Friday. Thomas was not given an injury designation. The Giants will officially release their inactives 90 minutes before kickoff. Who would replace Jermaine Eluemunor in the lineup? LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights The Cardinals produce another improbable victory behind a barrage of field goals, and the Dolphins finally hold their first lead of the season Getty Images Anything can happen in the National Football League and the kickoff to Week 7 of the 2026 season certainly solidified that idea. In the Chicago Bears 30-24 win over the New England Patriots , they triumphed despite allowing one of the most unique "Hail Mary" touchdown passes in recent memory. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye's 48-yard checkdown touchdown pass to running back Rhamondre Stevenson was the only touchdown pass in the last 20 years in the final 10 seconds of a half, 40-plus yards from the end zone on a throw of 10 or fewer air yards, per CBS Sports Research. What other craziness could happen during the rest of the NFL's Week 7 lineup? Daniel Jones cuts through Brian Flores' No. 1 Vikings defense The Minnesota Vikings are 5-0, and it is very much on the strength of defensive coordinator Brian Flores' aggressive unit. They are an immovable object. Flores' defense leads the NFL in: Scoring defense (12.8 points per game allowed) Third down defense (22.2% third down conversion rate allowed) Red zone defense (27.3% red zone touchdown rate allowed) Goal-to-go defense (33.3% goal-to-go touchdown rate allowed) Completion percentage allowed (53.2%) Touchdown-to-interception ratio allowed (3-6) Sack rate (9.8%) Pressure rate (46.4%) Blitz rate (69.8%) The Vikings' blitz rate of just under 70% (69.8%) is the highest by any team in any five-game span in the last 10 seasons, per CBS Sports Research. So how is that going to go for Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones in Week 7? Well, the bold prediction here is that he doesn't commit any turnovers and totals multiple touchdowns against Flores' unit. Jones' splits versus the blitz are the exact same in terms of yards per pass attempt this season (5.9), and he actually has a higher completion percentage, touchdown-to-interception ratio, and passer rating against the blitz in 2026. Jones also got to spend the second half of the 2024 season watching how Flores' unit operates up close in practice on a daily basis after Minnesota scooped him up for depth purposes after his New York Giants release. That practice experience against Flores will allow Jones to produce a clean, efficient performance. Daniel Jones vs. the blitz, 2026 season Pass attempts Completion percentage Pass yards per attempt Air yards per attempt Passer rating Bijan Robinson runs wild vs. the undefeated 49ers The undefeated San Francisco 49ers not only have a top-five scoring offense (29.5 points per game) but also a top-10 scoring defense (18.3 points allowed per game). That also extends to their run defense, which ranks as the seventh-best in football, allowing just 90.2 rushing yards per game. Bijan Robinson , who enters Week 7 leading the NFL with 785 yards from scrimmage, will go off for 150-plus rushing yards against San Francisco. He'll be well rested after having just 11 touches in Week 6, his fewest in a game since 2024, and Robinson will break what has been one of the 49ers' biggest strengths: their control of outside-zone runs. San Francisco has curbed outside-zone runs to just 3.2 yards per carry, the sixth-fewest in the NFL, and they are the only defense that hasn't allowed a gain of 10 or more yards on those runs, per the NFL's Next Gen Stats. They have also tackled rushers for a loss or no gain on 5 of 29 outside-zone carries, 17.2%. Robinson has 10 explosive runs (gains of 10 or more yards) on his 65 outside-zone carries, tied with Derrick Henry for the most in the league. He's also only been stuffed for no gain or a loss on 6 of his 65 outside-zone run carries. Robinson will repeatedly cook the 49ers, rushing to the outside, and he'll become not only the first player with over 100 yards rushing against San Francisco in 2026 but the first player to hit at least 150 yards rushing against San Francisco. Cardinals stun Broncos without scoring a touchdown The Arizona Cardinals (2-4) upset the preseason Super Bowl favorite Los Angeles Rams 18-16 in Week 6 as 13.5-point road underdogs, earning the second-largest upset win by any team in the last five seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. They accomplished that feat despite not finding the end zone one time. Arizona's 18 points came from six made field goals. The Cardinals host the Denver Broncos (4-2) while seeking their first win away from SoFi Stadium -- both of Arizona's wins have come on the road against the Rams and the Los Angeles Chargers . Denver enters Week 7 with a top 10 scoring defense (20.8 points per game, 10th in the NFL), but Arizona will upset them too for their first home win of the season. Even more impressively, the Cardinals will also beat the Broncos without scoring a touchdown, just like they did with the Rams in Week 6. How will that work? Arizona will pull off that near-impossibility thanks to the Broncos' offensive ceiling being capped by starting quarterback Bo Nix . Nix's 5.6 yards per pass attempt are the fewest in the NFL among quarterbacks to start every game in 2026, and his 4.9 air yards per pass attempt represent the shortest average pass length through six games in the last 20 seasons, according to CBS Sports Research. Not having to defend the deep ball will allow the Cardinals to get creatively aggressive on defense, and Nix will give Arizona's similarly shaky offense, led by journeyman Jacoby Brissett, enough latitude to win with six or seven made field goals and no touchdowns. J.J. McCarthy avoids being sacked vs. Will Anderson Jr., Texans The New York Giants have a new starting quarterback for Week 7 at the Houston Texans : Minnesota Vikings' 2024 10th overall pick castoff J.J. McCarthy . He ranked dead last in the NFL in completion percentage (57.6%), touchdown-to-interception ratio (11-12) and passer rating (72.6) among 33 qualified quarterbacks in 2025. He also had a 10% sack rate last season, the third highest in the entire league. However, McCarthy will not be sacked in his debut as the Giants' starting quarterback despite facing the Houston Texans and All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. , the NFL's sacks leader with 7.5 entering Week 7. How will that happen? Perhaps McCarthy has taken a big leap from 2025 to 2026. After checking in for a benched Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter in Week 6, McCarthy threw for 243 yards, the most by any quarterback in the play-by-play era (since 1991) who had no passing yards in the first three quarters, per CBS Sports Research. The humbling he took, being traded for a 2027 fifth-round pick, plus playing in a more simplistic offense in New York under offensive coordinator Matt Nagy and senior offensive assistant Greg Roman, will allow McCarthy to play a cleaner game in Week 7. That will help him avoid Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter's clutches as he avoids being sacked all game long. Dolphins take a lead for the first time this season The Miami Dolphins ' 2026 season is going exactly as one would expect for a franchise paying more for players not on its roster (an NFL-record $179 million in dead cap hits) than for the players on its roster ($156 million). They're 0-5 and have the NFL's worst scoring offense, averaging 14 points per game. They're also just the second team in the Super Bowl era (since 1966) to not have a lead in the first five games of a season, along with the 2005 Houston Texans, per CBS Sports Research. However, they will acquire their first lead in a game of the 2026 season against the New York Jets . The Jets have the worst red zone offense (37.5%) in the NFL, and they haven't scored a touchdown on their last seven red zone trips, which spans the last three games. New York has also been outscored 100-6 in the final two minutes of the first half under Aaron Glenn. Miami will capitalize on Glenn's end-of-the-first-half mismanagement and take a lead in a game for the first time this season. Nix has been a shell of himself through six weeks in the 2026 season, yet Denver is somehow 4-2 and favored on the road against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 7. Arizona is coming off a massive upset win on the road against the Los Angeles Rams, and while it may not be a playoff team, the Cardinals are not a pushover this season. Jacoby Brissett and Co. will have their work cut out for them against a Denver defense that is one of the best in the NFL. The Bronco offense (29th in success rate) hasn’t been able to get much going during this 4-2 start, but the defense has forced 10 turnovers and is allowing just 5.0 yards per play. The play on that side of the ball has stayed intact even with Pat Surtain II (missed the last two games) and Talanoa Hufanga (missed Week 6) injured. Arizona’s defense is one of the weaker ones that the Broncos have on the schedule, so Sean Payton may look to get his young quarterback going early on Sunday. Will it lead to a Denver win? All season long, the SI Betting team is sharing final score predictions for every NFL game, and we’re hoping it’ll help our readers decide on some spread, moneyline and total bets along the way. Plus, who doesn’t want to get an exact score bet right during the season? Denver is favored on the road, but can bettors trust this offense with Nix struggling? This spread suggests we could see a close game, so let’s dive right into my score prediction for this Week 7 battle. Broncos vs. Cardinals Score Prediction This week, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan continued his quest to bet on every NFL game in his Road to 272 column . In this matchup, he’s taking Denver to win and cover despite some early struggles on offense: You can throw all of the Broncos' middling metrics out the window, because no team has had a tougher schedule to begin the season than Denver. They've faced the Chiefs, Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks, and came out on the other end of that run with a 4-2 record. Despite playing that good a record, their defense still ranks sixth in opponent EPA per play and fifth in opponent success rate. Just imagine how good this defense is going to look when facing lower-tier competition. The Cardinals may be coming off the upset of the year over the Los Angeles Rams, but they enter this week ranking dead last in the NFL in net yards per play at -1.4. Their offense is solid at times, but their defense remains one of the worst units in the league. Give me the Broncos as road favorites. MacMillan has confidence in the Broncos this week, but I’m eyeing the UNDER with the Denver offense looking like one of the worst in the NFL. Arizona’s offense has been able to move the ball with Brissett under center, but Denver has been an elite defense the last few weeks, moving up into the top-12 in the league in points allowed, yards per play allowed, EPA/Play and success rate. The UNDER has hit in five of the Broncos’ six games this season, partially due to the fact that they’ve scored 23 or fewer points in five games and 20 or fewer points in four games. The Packers, winners of three in a row, are coming off a 23-13 defeat of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football. Meanwhile, Detroit, which spent Week 6 on its bye, defeated the Arizona Cardinals in Week 5, 45-21. Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 7 matchup with Green Bay. Christian Booher The Lions have their first chance to prove themselves in the NFC North Sunday, taking on a Green Bay Packers team that appears to be built to exploit Detroit's biggest weakness. Quarterback Jordan Love has been unafraid to test defenses down the field with wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. As a result, I think the Lions will try to dial up the pass-rush and try to get to Love before he has a chance to cut it loose. Offensively, the Lions need to get Jahmyr Gibbs going as the Packers did a good job of keeping him in check in their two meetings last year. Quarterback Jared Goff has been turnover-free through five games, and will need to keep that going to give his team the best chance to win. While the Lions have the ability to keep up in the event this game becomes a shootout, the Packers are uniquely equipped to attack the Lions' issues in coverage, both in the secondary and at linebacker. Green Bay makes one more play than Detroit, and hands Dan Campbell's team a crushing loss to start a crucial two-game stretch. Packers 31, Lions 28 The Detroit Lions have a big time test ahead of themselves on Sunday against the Green Bay Packers. The Packers not only are red hot and winners of three in a row. But they're also due to receive a big boost to their run game with the return of Pro Bowl back Josh Jacobs. In addition, Green Bay receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are playing some of the best football of their NFL careers. Consequently, Kelvin Sheppard's defense won't have it easy in this Week 7 divisional affair. Yet, the Lions' defense will be in the best shape it's been all season due to the return of Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch. He should provide a major boost to the team's secondary and put it in a stronger position to limit the productivity of Watson and Golden. I think Detroit's pass defense holds up just enough and Jared Goff and the offense come through in the fourth quarter, leading Dan Campbell's squad to its fourth victory of the season. Lions 31, Packers 24 John Maakaron The Lions return to action after a much needed week off. The Packers are visiting Ford Field missing a few key players, but will have running back Josh Jacobs in the lineup. If the defensive line can have another strong performance, Jordan Love will not have ample time to find his key targets. Tight end Tucker Kraft could be in line for a big game, but Detroit’s offense should keep the momentum from the first quarter of the season rolling. Sam LaPorta might just also have himself a productive afternoon, given the noise he created and wanting to prove he deserves a lucrative new contract. Emmett Matasovsky The Lions start divisional play with the Green Bay Packers this week, and it sees the return of Brian Branch and Josh Jacobs for their respective teams. That makes this week even more intriguing. It will be interesting to see how, or if, the bye week has given Detroit time to somewhat fix its porous secondary. The return of Branch will give fans a glimpse as to how this secondary should operate, but the boundary corner issues could make this discussion irrelevant. Green Bay is a hard team to gauge, even before factoring in the wild card element that it is a divisional game in the NFC North. The Lions, on fresh legs and with momentum, alongside a rowdy Ford Field crowd, take the win to open the second half of the season. picks.blurb: Packers-Lions Prediction: Will Green Bay Beat Odds So It Can Beat Rivals? The Packers are coming off a Sunday night home game. The Lions are coming off a Sunday at their homes with their bye week. So, Detroit – in a huge NFC North game, mind you, that could have playoff ramifications – has been given by the league a home game and a week of rest. Will it matter? Here are our predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Lions Prediction Since the start of the 2020 season, teams with a home game after their bye are 63-41, according to Stathead. That’s an enormous advantage. Will that alone decide the game? Probably not. But in a game between two quality teams – the Lions are 3.5-point favorites – it might not take much to be the tipping point. Eight consecutive games at Ford Field between the teams ended with a one-score differential; the last exception was in 2017, when Brett Hundley was the Packers’ quarterback. Both teams are going to score points. A lot of points. The over/under of 55.5 points is the highest on the board at FanDuel. The Lions on offense have been a well-oiled machine. It tallied 30 points in five of six games this season and is second in the league in scoring. Quarterback Jared Goff hasn’t thrown an interception all season. He is surrounded by probably the best quartet in the league with receivers Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams, running back Jahmyr Gibbs and tight end Sam LaPorta. Green Bay’s defense was great last week against the Dak Prescott-led Cowboys passing attack, but it didn’t have to contend with a back like Gibbs, who is arguably the best in the league – especially at home. The Packers have been hit and miss on offense – which is about what you’d expect for a team with a big-time quarterback and two big-play receivers but with an inconsistent offensive line and an unimaginably bad running game. The matchup is favorable, though, because the Lions’ defense has been terrible. It ranks 30th in points allowed and 32nd in total defense. At its current clip, it will threaten the 2011 Packers as the worst pass defense in NFL history. For the Lions, the best defense has been a good offense. They are 3-2 despite allowing 20 touchdowns. According to Stats Perform’s Opta data, they are the first team in NFL history to allow 20 offensive touchdowns and have a winning record through five games. Ultimately, three big issues stand the Packers’ way. One, they have struggled to protect Love. Well, the Lions lead the NFL in sacks even while playing one fewer game than most teams. Can Green Bay’s tackles overcome the noise to keep Aidan Hutchinson away from Love? Two, they have struggled to pressure the quarterback at times. Goff is an elite quarterback when given time. As coach Matt LaFleur said this week, “It’s hard for a quarterback to throw when he’s on his back.” Can the Packers put Goff on his back enough? Furthermore, the Green Bay defense will line up without Micah Parsons, Edgerrin Cooper and Zaire Franklin. And, finally, there’s this festering problem: The Packers have fatal flaws they haven’t solved. Love has been stymied by 19 drops; no other quarterback has more than 11. They lead the league in penalties and penalty yards. Love has faced the third-most pressures. “The simple stuff, whether from scheme-wise or the understanding of what we’re trying to get done, when you have some mistakes that can lead to negative plays, that’s the stuff we got to clean up and be better at,” Love said. It’s those things that will put the Packers at a disadvantage in every big game – no matter the location or scheduling quirk – until they get them fixed. Ultimately, the team that makes the fewest mistakes will win. Based on the first five games, it’s hard to believe that will be the Packers. Bill Huber’s Prediction: Lions 31, Packers 27. Bill’s Record: 3-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Lions Prediction The Packers have lost too many games like these in recent years, which have caused them to travel the long road in the postseason. In 2024, they lost all but one division game, which played a significant factor in them being the seventh seed in the NFC playoffs. Last year’s late-season debacle in Chicago essentially sealed their fate that the wild-card meeting rematch would be at Soldier Field instead of the friendly confines of Lambeau Field. Simply put, the Packers need to knock off the Lions on the road on Sunday to keep pace with those in front of them and remain in position to be a legitimate NFC North contender. In a game where points should be scored in bunches, one mistake could be the difference. Who do you trust more to play clean and disciplined? Dan Campbell's Lions or Matt LaFleur's Packers? That, combined with the Lions being at home off a bye, gives them the nod. Jacob’s Prediction: Lions 34, Packers 31 Jacob’s Record: 3-3. Even with drops (bad) and interference penalties drawn (good), the Packers' Matthew Golden is having the biggest breakout season by a receiver in more than a decade. ⬇️ https://t.co/EsADb0e8gG Published 8 hours ago BILL HUBER Bill Huber, who has covered the Green Bay Packers since 2008, is the publisher of Packers On SI, a Sports Illustrated channel. Most recently, the Matt LaFleur-led squad dispatched of the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football, 23-13. It marked the third consecutive game in which Green Bay held its opponent to 14 or fewer points. And on the season, the Packers’ defense – coordinated by former Arizona Cardinals head coach Jonathan Gannon – has allowed the 10th-fewest points in the NFL (20.8/game). Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the ball, Green Bay – led under center by sixth-year passer Jordan Love – has scored the 10th-fewest points in the game (21.2/game). Through six weeks, Love has also completed just 59.7 percent of his pass attempts. If the season ended today, it'd rank as his lowest completion percentage as a starting quarterback in the NFL. Yet, multiple Green Bay pass-catchers have flourished, most notably wide receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Watson, now in his fifth NFL season, has already amassed as many touchdowns as last season (six) and nearly as many receptions (29) and reception yards as he did a year ago (538). The former second-round pick secured 35 catches and 611 yards in 10 games a season ago. Meanwhile, Golden, Green Bay's first-round pick in 2025, has already surpassed all his receiving totals from his rookie campaign. He's already racked up 30 catches, 501 yards and three touchdowns amid a career breakout season. And just like Watson, he's well on pace for a 1,000-yard receiving campaign. Consequently, both Watson and Golden possess the potential to wreak havoc against the Lions’ secondary, even with Pro Bowl safety Brian Branch back in the fold for Detroit. In addition to Watson and Golden, the Lions will also likely have their hands full with Packers running back Josh Jacobs. The Pro Bowler returns to the lineup after spending the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner exempt list for an offseason domestic abuse incident. Jacobs, who's coming off a 929-yard, 13-touchdown rushing campaign in 2025, should provide an immediate boost to Green Bay's league-worst ground game. In case you were wondering, the Packers have compiled a measly 359 total rushing yards through the season's first six games. Expect Jacobs, along with Watson and Golden, to give Kelvin Sheppard's defense its fair share of fits on Sunday. However, at this present juncture, I'm still willing to give the Lions a 60 percent chance to pull off the Week 7 victory at home. picks.blurb: Roundtable: Lions Week 7 Preview Against Packers Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions OnSI staff previews the Detroit Lions Week 7 matchup with the Green Bay Packers. 1. How do you see the Lions’ Week 7 game against the Packers playing out? Vito Chirco: I believe the Lions will be tested all game long against the Packers. To me, Green Bay is a formidable opponent, and might be even stronger now with the return of Pro Bowl running back Josh Jacobs. So, if the Lions play anything less than their “A game,” they're likely going to be in trouble and end up on the losing end. But, I envision a solid enough effort from Dan Campbell's squad in this Week 7 divisional affair. I believe with Brian Branch back in the starting lineup, the Lions will deliver one key stop and Jared Goff and the offense will come through in the fourth quarter. The Lions come out on top in what will be a highly contested game from start to finish. Emmett Matasovsky: With Cade Mays and Josh Jacobs both active on offense for their respective squads, I foresee a shootout. The Lions get Brian Branch back for some desperately needed help on defense, but the question becomes if that is enough. The Lions offense, on fresh legs after an extremely strong start to the year, is expected to be deadly. Any given player or star can produce, and it is a battle to stick with Jahmyr Gibbs for the whole event. I see a Motown win at the very end. Christian Booher : This is a great opportunity for the Lions to prove that they belong in the conversation for the NFC North title. Getting Branch and Mays back will be huge wins, and both players will be able to make a huge impact. Detroit's defense is the biggest factor in Sunday's game. The Packers have shown that they're not afraid to take deep shot after deep shot, and the Lions' secondary has struggled as one of the league's worst pass defenses. I think it's a shootout, with Green Bay getting one more big play than Detroit and stealing the win. 2. Who will be the Lions’ game MVP? Chirco : I'm going to go with Jahmyr Gibbs. I know that the Packers’ pass defense is one of the best in the league, so I think the Lions will need a big game from Gibbs in order to secure the Week 7 victory. And I believe Gibbs will deliver just that for Detroit, helping Dan Campbell's team eke out its fourth win of the season. Matasovsky : The MVP will be Jahmyr Gibbs. Gibbs had 200 yards from scrimmage and got the full week to rest up, along with regaining Cade Mays on the offensive line. Mays is expected to be a tangible upgrade from Juice Scruggs, and the former second-rounder already did an admirable job paving the way to open the year. Expect at least 150 yards from scrimmage for Sonic, if not over 200 yards. Booher : I think it will be Aidan Hutchinson. The Michigan product is one of the top pass-rushers in the league, and against a team that could decimate Detroit's secondary, Hutchinson could change the game by getting to Jordan Love. I expect him to have a massive impact against a struggling Packers' offensive line. 3. Do you think the Lions’ secondary will struggle against the Packers’ passing attack? Chirco : I think there certainly will be moments. Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are a formidable pass-caching duo, and they've been torching pass defenses for weeks now. And even though it's great to have Brian Branch back, Detroit is still lacking a bonafide No. 1 cornerback. With that said, I expect Watson and Golden to both deliver strong showings in this Week 7 tilt. Matasovsky : In all passing yards per game statistics, be it from this season or the last three games, the Packers rank among the top 10 in passing yards for the NFL. The Lions secondary, even in one of their best games, let Jacoby Brissett throw for a season-high yardage. The obvious answer is yes. Brian Branch coming back will be huge, but the Lions have already lost a prime piece that would rotate from the re-activation of Branch, as Avonte Maddox’s season ended from injury. Branch can only be in one place at a time, and when there are multiple missed assignments in coverage each play, breakdowns will happen. Booher : I do think the Lions are going to struggle on Sunday against Green Bay's passing attack. Green Bay is uniquely designed to give the Lions problems, with an array of weapons like Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and tight end Tucker Kraft. I believe the Packers are going to test the Lions early, and as a result a big defensive play could help swing momentum. Because the Lions have struggled so much in the secondary, the onus is on the pass-rush to get home and make everyone's life easier. 4. How messy were TE Sam LaPorta’s comments this week? Chirco : To me, they were very messy and uncalled for. I'll take it a step further and say they were tone deaf. LaPorta has to be able to “read the room” better and know that those comments are only going to piss off the Lions fanbase and make him look like an individual who is out of touch with reality (especially considering the economic issues in today's world). LaPorta lost himself a lot of supporters with those comments, and he just better hope now he “balls out” the rest of the season. Matasovsky : In the media, it is a scandal. The Iowa product said the quiet part out loud about his frustrating contract negotiations after his best game of the season. It is (justifiably) one of, if not the top, media story of the week. In the locker room, I do not think there are many eyebrows being raised or heads being turned. Those that are close with LaPorta in Allen Park’s facility have likely heard the same frustrations, probably with more expletives thrown in. It is messy, but I doubt it is a locker room distraction or the beginning crack of a broken locker room. It is, like I said earlier, a player saying the quiet part out loud about their negotiations. Booher : I was not expecting those comments because of how the Lions have traditionally handled those conversations. LaPorta does have every right to be upset with the way things are going, but that should be a conversation for the organization, not a larger audience. I think Mike Valenti's point on it was very accurate. It was a tone-deaf argument from LaPorta and insulting to fans. However, he's justifiably a huge part of the organization with how well he's played since being drafted, and as a result some of his frustrations are understood. 5. What do you want to see from safety Brian Branch? Chirco : I want to see him log “competitive” snaps in his 2026 season debut. And when I say competitive, I mean I want to see him running around the field and being a nuisance against both the run and the pass. When Branch is at his best, that is exactly what he brings to the table. So, if he can make a couple run stops and deflect a pass or two, I think it'd be a solid outing from the Pro Bowl safety. Matasovsky : Not to set lofty goals, but three interceptions. Just kidding. I want to see a player that has a good range of motion and full trust in his legs when it comes time to plant to jump, or to leave his feet when diving for a tackle. On top of that, I want to see a more informed secondary in terms of communication with Branch on the field. In coverage, I want to see the Alabama product staying close enough, if not fully stride-for-stride. In essence, I want to see signs of the former Lions second-round pick being healthy. The final, and most important, thing I want to see from him on Sunday is him walking up the Ford Field tunnel postgame in full pads and with a clean bill of health. Booher : For me, I would just like to see Branch be able to play and move around in some capacity. away.headline: Green Bay Packers RB Josh Jacobs contrite as he prepares to play again amid ongoing NFL investigation
away.blurb: The NFL is still investigating Jacobs over the incident, so the league still could hand out more discipline to the three-time Pro Bowl running back. But for now, Jacobs is eligible to play again for the Packers after missing the first six games of the season. “I thought I’d be playing sooner,” Jacobs said. “But, you know, the optics of everything, I understand the other side. For me, like I said, I’m just grateful to be able to play. It was one of them things where I didn’t want to sit the whole year and then figure it out. I’m just grateful to be back on the team and to be back playing.” Today's E-Editions Chicago Tribune Advertise with Us Advertise with Us Branded Content Paid Partner Content Print (Opens in new window) Print Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email 🪄 Harry Houdini's great escapes GREEN BAY — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs expressed contrition as he returned to practice Wednesday and talked with reporters for the first time since pleading no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend during which she said he threw her to the ground. “Obviously, man, I’m remorseful and sorry for putting this team in this situation,” Jacobs said. “Sometimes when you go through life, situations occur and a four-second, three-second decision can alter your life, honestly.” Jacobs was removed this week from the commissioner’s exempt list, which had prevented him from playing or practicing. The NFL had placed Jacobs on that list Aug. 30 , shortly after charges were filed against him . He pleaded no contest last month to misdemeanor counts of battery and criminal damage to property. The Packers (4-2) face the Lions on Sunday in Detroit. Jacobs was arrested May 26 , three days after police officers came to his Wisconsin home to investigate a disturbance. According to police, the woman told them that Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground. Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head. The criminal complaint against him noted that a surveillance video from the camera system in their garage corroborated the woman’s statement. Both Jacobs and the victim have gone to court attempting to have that video and other evidence sealed permanently . Jacobs declined to discuss the specifics of his case but said he hopes to use the situation as an opportunity to grow into a better person. “You never want to be in this situation, but just me being honest, for my life, it was probably one of the best things to ever happen to me,” Jacobs said. “I say that because it gave me a chance to sit down and reevaluate what’s important and what I want my life to look like, and what do I want people to know me for. away.blurb: Packers rule out Zaire Franklin, list four questionable vs. Lions | Week 7 Injury Report Skip to main content Primary nav News Evan Siegle, packers.com LB Zaire Franklin GREEN BAY – Packers have officially ruled out linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) and listed four questionable for Sunday's NFC North matchup with the Detroit Lions. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. Veteran Laken Tomlinson has started the past three games at left guard. The Packers didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Jordan Love (back), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), and receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Savion Williams (ankle). Lions safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were full participants in practice this week but are both questionable for Sunday. The four questionable are guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), receiver Bo Melton (back) and defensive tackle Jordon Riley (Achilles), who's currently on the physically unable to perform list and would need to be added to the 53-man roster to play against the Lions. Sunday will mark only the second game Franklin has missed in nine NFL seasons, snapping a streak of 48 consecutive games played dating back to Week 8 of the 2023 season when the former All-Pro linebacker sat out against Carolina with a knee injury. The Packers could have reinforcements on the way up front against the Lions and star running back Jahmyr Gibbs, as Riley appears to be nearing a return. The third-year defensive tackle has practiced in a limited capacity the past two weeks, his first on-field work since tearing his Achilles last December. Banks has been out since injuring his toe against the New York Jets in Week 2. The 6-foot-5, 325-pound guard was also battling knee tendinitis at the time of his toe injury. Veteran Laken Tomlinson has started the past three games at left guard. The Packers didn't issue a game status for the following players who will be available: quarterback Jordan Love (back), edge rusher Lukas Van Ness (illness), cornerback Brandon Cisse (shoulder/neck), defensive tackle Anthony Campbell (ankle), and receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Matthew Golden (shoulder) and Savion Williams (ankle). Lions safety Brian Branch (Achilles) and center Cade Mays (wrist) were full participants in practice this week but are both questionable for Sunday. Cornerback Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) does not have a game status and will play. ** Designated to Return from Injured Reserve - Currently within 21-day practice window * The Lions did not practice Wednesday; Practice participation designations for that day are based on estimations. news Packers list five questionable, rule out four vs. Cowboys | Week 6 Injury Report CB Brandon Cisse (hip) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday night news Packers list three questionable, two doubtful vs. Bears | Week 5 Injury Report DT Javon Hargrave (toe) added to injury report, questionable for Sunday news Packers rule out four, list two questionable vs. Buccaneers | Week 4 Injury Report OL Aaron Banks, Jacob Monk ruled out; LB Edgerrin Cooper questionable for Sunday Veteran linebacker won’t play Sunday after suffering injury at Thursday’s practice Wes Hodkiewicz packers.com senior writer Head Coach Matt LaFleur told reporters on Friday morning that Franklin took a knee to his shin during a collision at practice Thursday. home.headline: Packers Get Good Injury News on Explosive WR Duo Before Lions Game
home.blurb: Watson was listed with an ankle injury, while Golden appeared with a shoulder issue. Both were estimated limited participants as Green Bay conducted a walkthrough rather than a full practice. The team's injury concerns extend beyond those two receivers, however. Love was also listed as limited Wednesday because of a back injury, while fellow wideout Savion Williams appeared with an ankle injury. The importance of having both receivers available becomes even clearer when considering what Detroit is preparing to defend. There's also the potential return of running back Josh Jacobs , who resumed practicing this week after being removed from the commissioner's exempt list. With the Packers visiting Detroit at Ford Field on Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET, LaFleur's latest update suggests Green Bay should have its top two passing-game weapons available for a pivotal divisional matchup. home.headline: Jordan Love, Christian Watson among Packers off injury report and set to play vs. Lions
home.blurb: Earlier this week, Packers quarterback Jordan Love told reporters he would be available to play on Sunday, despite being listed as limited on Wednesday with a back issue. Receivers Christian Watson (ankle), Savion Williams (ankle), and Matthew Golden (shoulder) are also off the injury report and are all set to play, despite being listed as limited all week. Guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe), receiver Bo Melton (back), cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring), and defensive tackle Jordan Riley (Achilles) are all questionable. Head coach Matt LaFleur noted earlier on Friday that linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin) is out after suffering an injury on Thursday .
